findings.title: Subagent-wait toggle chevron becomes permanently invisible
findings.failure: `.chat-tool-row__chevron` now defaults to `opacity: 0`, and every rule that reveals it again is scoped to `.chat-inline-disclosure` (hover, focus-within, aria-expanded) or to file and subagent rows. ChatSubagentWaitLine (chat-handoff-sessions.tsx) puts the same chevron class inside `.chat-subagent-wait__toggle`, which is not a `.chat-inline-disclosure`. Before this change that chevron showed at 0.55 opacity. When a handoff waits on several sessions, the 'Waiting on N sessions' toggle no longer shows a chevron in any state (collapsed, expanded, hovered or focused), so nothing on screen says the line can open or close.

findings.title: Grid on .chat-activity-group stretches the bubble-mode working pill and summaries to full width
findings.failure: `.chat-activity-group` is now `display: grid`. In bubble mode, `.chat-activity-group--bubble > .chat-activity-group__summary` sets `width: auto`, which overrides the `width: fit-content` from `.chat-inline-disclosure`. A grid item with `width: auto` stretches to fill its column; before, as an inline-flex child of a block container, it shrank to fit its content. The live 'working' bubble summary has a border, an elevated background, an 18px radius and centered dots. It now draws as a wide bar across the whole activity group (up to the 760px max width) instead of a compact pill. Completed bubble summaries likewise get a full-width click target and focus outline.

findings.title: Tool row text stays highlighted after a mouse click
findings.failure: The new `.chat-tool-msg-summary:focus-within { color: var(--text) }` rule matches any focus inside the row, including focus from a mouse click. When a user clicks a tool row to expand or collapse it, or clicks its file link, the button keeps focus, so that row stays in full text color while every other row stays muted. It keeps the hover look until the user clicks somewhere else. The existing focus-visible rule kept the highlight for keyboard focus only.

findings.title: Sterile probe env rejects version-manager Node shims (Volta, asdf, mise)
findings.failure: Each PATH candidate is probed with buildProbeEnv(env), which keeps only SystemRoot/WINDIR/TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR and drops HOME, PATH, VOLTA_HOME, ASDF_DATA_DIR and similar. On a Bun-hosted install where Node comes from a version manager (a common setup), the `node` on PATH is a shim that needs HOME or its own env vars to pick a real Node version. Without them the shim exits non-zero (for example 'No version is set for command node' or a Volta home error), so every candidate is skipped and null is cached. isToolSearchCodeModeSupported() then returns false and Tool Search quietly drops from code mode to tools mode under Bun, even though a compatible Node is installed. resolveTestNodeExecPath (which used to probe with the full process.env) now throws 'Unable to locate a Node executable' on the same machines.

findings.title: Negative resolution is cached for the life of the process
findings.failure: When no candidate succeeds, null is cached under a key built only from the platform, runtime version, flag, PATH and PATHEXT. That happens if Node is installed or upgraded after the Gateway starts, or if one cold-start probe hits the 5 s timeout on a loaded machine. Every later resolveToolSearchConfig call then reports code mode unsupported and silently uses tools mode, and tool_search_code keeps failing with 'requires an installed Node runtime', until the Bun-hosted process restarts. No warning names the cause.

findings.title: Retained search reader skips persisted corruption quarantine on every request after the first
findings.failure: Previously every keyword/curated/index-state/vector request opened a fresh connection through openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly, which runs revalidateAgentDatabaseTerminalOpen and readOpenClawDatabaseQuarantineFailure and throws when the database has been quarantined as corrupt. With retainOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly the cached scope reuses its idle reader and only calls assertAgentDatabaseTerminalOpenAllowed, whose latch is a per-thread global singleton that the search worker thread does not register. Once the Gateway (another thread) quarantines a damaged memory/agent database, the search worker keeps serving recall and search results from the quarantined file instead of failing with the quarantine error; because each recall turn refreshes the idle timer, under steady traffic this can last indefinitely.

findings.title: Failed search keeps its broken connection for later requests
findings.failure: The finally block always just releases the borrow, even when the request threw (e.g. SqliteSchemaMismatchError 'schema admission changed; retry the request', SQLITE_CORRUPT, or an I/O error). The cached scope's own read() path discards the connection on error for exactly this reason, but retain() has no such handling, so the next search request on that worker reuses the same connection and can fail the same way, whereas the old per-request open recovered on the next request.

findings.title: Overlapping full-width footer swallows pointer input on the transcript's bottom band, including its scrollbar
findings.failure: The new negative margin-top pulls .chat-footer (position: relative, full pane width, no pointer-events: none) 28px (35px at corner scale 1.25) up over .chat-thread-viewport, and as the later positioned sibling it paints and hit-tests above the transcript. The transcript's scrollbar sits at the pane edge (scrollbar-gutter both-edges), outside the centered composer, so the bottom 28-35px of the scrollbar track, and on Windows/Linux classic scrollbars the down-arrow button, now lie under the transparent footer: clicking or dragging there hits the footer instead of the scrollbar. Likewise, while scrolled mid-conversation, links, buttons and text in messages passing through that band beside the composer's rounded corners are visible but not clickable or selectable. Wheel input is forwarded, but mouse clicks and drags are not.

findings.title: Full-pane history-error view gets the footer overlap without compensating bottom padding
findings.failure: The extra bottom padding was added only to .chat-thread-viewport/.chat-thread, but the footer's negative margin applies whatever sits above it. When history fails with an empty transcript, the fallback .chat-history-error (an overflow:auto scrollport whose stage has min-height 260px and only 24px padding) occupies that slot. The footer now covers its bottom 28-35px: in a short pane where the stage scrolls, scrolling to the end leaves the last few pixels of the Retry control under the composer, and in taller panes the centered error art/text is centered in a box that extends behind the composer, so it sits visibly lower than the space actually visible above the composer.

findings.title: Settled-view bounding throws on messages without a valid numeric timestamp
findings.failure: boundSettledFinalizationMessages builds a synthetic entry with `new Date(message.timestamp).toISOString()` for every message in the frozen settled view (only to fill a field the selector never reads). The settled view now comes from activeSession.messages, which for context-engine sessions is whatever the engine's assemble() returned; assembled messages are not normalized and a plugin-produced summary/custom message without a timestamp (or with a non-date string) makes toISOString throw RangeError('Invalid time value'). prepareEmbeddedAttemptHistory then fails, the isolated finalizer errors, and the turn ends as 'settled-turn finalization failed — preserving failed recovery' with no final answer, where before the change finalization rehydrated the transcript and succeeded.

findings.title: Compaction summary in the settled view loses its required-boundary treatment
findings.failure: Every settled message, including a compactionSummary produced by compaction during the source attempt, is wrapped as an entry of type 'message'. selectBoundedModelRequests only pins entries of type 'compaction'/'reset' as the boundary, so under byte pressure (e.g. screenshot-heavy turns exceeding contextTokenBudget*8 bytes) the summary at the head of the view is the first thing cut. The finalizer then answers without the summarized earlier context, whereas transcript hydration always retained the compaction boundary.

findings.title: Desktop size select keeps 88px width but now carries the shared select's wide chevron padding, truncating its value on touch
findings.failure: The desktop sizing select (non-menu presentation, including the desktop-touch-toolbar in document mode) stays at a fixed 88px but now takes settings-select chrome: --field-padding-inline (10px) on the left and calc(26px + 0.5em) on the right (36px in browsers without base-select), plus borders, instead of the old 0 6px padding and 12px type. That leaves about 40-42px for the value. On a coarse-pointer device the global 16px !important select floor applies, so 'Actual' (and 'Match') no longer fit and render as 'Actu...' / 'Matc...' via the new one-line clamp (or are clipped in Firefox). Longer translations are truncated even at desktop type size. The user cannot read the current sizing mode in the touch toolbar.

findings.title: createdVia spawn skip drops restart resume for dashboard-key spawned sessions whose requester is never marked
findings.failure: restartResumeSkipReason now returns "subagent" for any entry with createdVia "spawn". resolveRootSubagentRequester only walks parents for isSubagentSessionKey keys, so a running dashboard-key spawned session (for example an independent visible session from sessions-spawn-visible, or a child spawned without a yield batch) is enumerated as its own root at shutdown. It passes the key-only check, then gets skipped as "subagent" once the entry is read at marker write time, and again in the startup orphan and skip checks. Its requester is not marked either, because it is not running and has no requesterYieldBatch wake. After a restart or crash, nobody receives the resume input: the user's interrupted turn in that session stays stopped with no notice, where it previously got its own resume input.

findings.title: Quiet or intentional non-delivery settlements are recorded as child-result delivery failures
findings.failure: The new failure branch fires whenever outcome?.delivered !== true, which includes outcome === undefined. requester-settle-wake.ts calls completeBatch with no outcome for quiet settlements: cancellation already owns the result (isBatchDeliveryClosed, e.g. kill reconciliation or suppressCompletionDelivery), no remaining completion rows, no child owing a completion message, and requester turnover. It also calls it for intentional non-delivery such as store replaced or private requester replaced. For a yield batch, each of these now writes an error terminal with "The child result couldn't be delivered..." onto a requester that is still parked. It does this through the exact-run path, which can, for example, beat the kill path's terminal. For stable batches without requesterRunId, it appends a visible run-failed notice to the conversation even after the user has moved on or stopped it. Users see a spurious failure for work that was cancelled or intentionally not delivered.

findings.title: Sweeper now settles retired yielded runs as errors when child authority is not 'verified'
findings.failure: The sweeper no longer gates on (!executionRetired || waitForMessage), and every run restored after a restart is retired, so every restored yielded run reaches settleUnreachableYieldedSubagentRun. That function now converts 'continuable' into 'unreachable' whenever resolveSubagentYieldWaitSource returns undefined. That happens when getRecordedSubagentChildAuthority is not 'verified', for example a legacy-unverified record whose childSessionIdentity lacks lifecycleRevision. It also happens when a grandchild's completionRequesterLifecycleRevision or requesterRunId does not line up with the parent run. A nested child that is still waiting for its own descendants is then force-completed with "Descendant completion can no longer continue this yielded requester." Before this change it stayed parked. Startup resolveSessionYieldWait likewise marks it 'unreachable' and records a failure terminal.

findings.title: Sidecar churn during guarded copy now aborts the snapshot instead of retrying
findings.failure: copySourceFile pins the source fd, resolves realpath, then lets copyRootFileSync re-open the path by name and compare identity. If the file is deleted or replaced between the pin and the helper's open, the helper throws an FsSafeError (not-found or identity mismatch) rather than SqliteSourceChangedError. prepareArtifactPreservingCopy only retries SqliteSourceChangedError, so the snapshot fails on the first try. The previous code copied from the pinned fd and turned drift into a retryable SqliteSourceChangedError, and the async sibling (copyPreparedLocation) still does this through its finally-block identity check. The common trigger is a database in rollback (DELETE) journal mode being written during the snapshot: SQLite deletes and recreates <db>-journal on every commit. The WAL file can also be removed when the last connection closes. A commit landing in that window makes update candidate-state inspection, update generation hashing (readCommittedContent), state ownership checks, or artifact-preserving state reads fail with a raw fs-safe error, where they used to retry and settle. The worker's contention classifier also no longer labels the failure retryable.

findings.title: Every hydration transaction starts/stops the shared native GC profiler, not just slow ones
findings.failure: startSqliteStatementTiming(true) runs for every transaction under an inherited sessions.transcript-hydration.* owner, regardless of whether it ends up slow. Each call to observeGcSamples either creates a new GCProfiler plus a setInterval timer, or, when worker-memory/diagnostic-gc already subscribe, forces drain(true) (native profiler stop + restart and a synchronous fan-out to the other subscribers, which may postMessage) at both start and stop. The gc-observer explicitly limits restarts to about once per second; a worker serving many hydration reads now restarts it twice per transaction inside the read hold, adding CPU and latency to every hydration even though the GC figure is only ever logged for slow holds.

findings.title: Hovering any external link makes the Gateway GET the full URL, consuming one-time/action links
findings.failure: resolveHoverPreviewTarget accepts every http(s) cross-origin anchor that isn't one of a few hard-coded markers (only the wizard sign-in button was opted out via data-link-reader-external). A chat transcript or settings page containing a magic-login, email-confirmation, password-reset, unsubscribe, invite-accept or OAuth authorize link (with its token in path/query) will, on a 250 ms mouse hover or keyboard focus, be sent to controlUi.linkPreview and fetched by the Gateway with a plain GET. Sites that act on GET consume the one-time token or perform the action (confirm/unsubscribe), so when the operator later clicks the link it reports 'link expired/already used', or the action happened without a click. The change itself recognizes this hazard for the wizard sign-in URL but leaves all other authorization/action links in transcripts exposed.

findings.title: Review of an archived sandboxed session now throws instead of returning an empty/unavailable diff
findings.failure: Archiving a session with a managed worktree keeps entry.worktree and spawnedCwd but removes the worktree (registry removedAt set, snapshotRef kept); the local workspace projection row is only deleted later by retention expiry. Opening Review on such an archived session now finds the projection row, matches the binding, then hits `worktree.removedAt !== undefined` and throws "Local workspace review owner changed". Before the change the missing checkout made loadCheckoutRevision return undefined and sessions.diff returned an empty not_git result; now the operator sees an RPC error in the Review panel for every archived sandboxed session until the projection expires (about 31 days).

findings.title: Accepted base is HEAD at sandbox preparation, so pre-existing branch commits disappear from All changes and history
findings.failure: The projection's base_commit is set at first sandbox prepare to the worktree's current `HEAD` (local-workspace-state.ts prepare), not to the merge base with the default branch. When the session's worktree already had commits before the sandbox projection was created (for example the session ran unsandboxed and committed, or the operator committed in the worktree before the first sandboxed turn), Review now passes that HEAD as baseCommit: All changes, aheadCount and the commit list omit those commits, and scope=commit for them returns unknown_commit, although they are part of the branch the PR row/publication diffs against the default-branch merge base.

findings.title: Pending/conflicted base refresh leaves stale base_commit while canonical checkout already contains upstream
findings.failure: During refresh_base the staged result is applied to the canonical worktree first (pending_target switches to projection) and base_commit is only advanced after the projection side applies without conflicts. If the projection side conflicts, the row stays pending with the old base_commit while the canonical checkout already holds the upstream content. Review now forces the old accepted base, so it shows every upstream-only file as a task change (the very symptom being fixed), even when the default-branch refs are current and the previous ref-based base would have hidden them.

findings.title: Empty top-level draft description discards the manifest's agent description
findings.failure: createClawDraft seeds the draft with description: "". If the agent writes the description only in the CLAW.md frontmatter (agent.description), as the draft-format reference example does, and leaves the top-level field empty, `choices?.description ?? proposal.description ?? manifest.agent.description` stops at "" because ?? does not skip empty strings. The code then sets manifest.agent.description to undefined. The review shows an empty description, and if the creator publishes without retyping it, the package has no description.

findings.title: Review always overwrites the agent display name with the package slug
findings.failure: applyClawDraftChoices unconditionally sets manifest.agent.name = name, where name is the lowercase package slug, even when no choices are given. A draft that declares agent.name: "Portable Agent" (as in the documented format) is published with agent.name "portable-agent-slug", so installers see the slug instead of the author's chosen display name.

findings.title: ClawHub identity failures are reported as a draft-content problem
findings.failure: reviewClawDraft and publishClawDraft first call /api/v1/whoami through fetchClawHubJson. An expired or revoked `clawhub login` token (401), a rate limit, or a network error throws a ClawHubRequestError, not a ClawProjectError. draftError then returns the generic "The Claw draft could not be processed. Check its contents and try again." The creator is sent to edit a valid draft instead of signing in again or retrying.

findings.title: Definitive publish rejections are reported as unconfirmed with no reason
findings.failure: The catch around the POST to /api/v1/packages turns every error into publication_unconfirmed, including definite HTTP rejections such as 409 (version already exists), 400 (validation), or 403 (handle not allowed). For example, a creator who publishes 0.1.0 again is told publication "was not confirmed" and to check ClawHub, but never learns that the version already exists or which field ClawHub rejected.

findings.title: prepare_pr guidance still tells the model an explicit refresh imports the newer PR head and is acknowledged with expectedHeadCommit, contradicting the now-enabled bound refresh_base
findings.failure: In a prepared-PR session with refresh_base available, the prepare_pr paragraph (unchanged) says 'An explicit refresh of the bound PR integrates its newer head' and 'repeat with conflictsResolved: true and expectedHeadCommit set to the returned headCommit', while refresh_base now accepts bound PRs but never imports the head and only acknowledges via baseCommit. A model following the prepare_pr text calls refresh_base to pick up another writer's commits (nothing imported; next publish fails push_rejected) or acknowledges refresh_base conflicts with expectedHeadCommit and no baseCommit, which throws 'The pending source integration changed; call refresh_base again'.

findings.title: Unmarked configs with a deliberate exclusive plugins.allow get skill-workshop added and are never stamped
findings.failure: The allowlist rule treats any unmarked config whose previous and next plugins.allow both omit skill-workshop as 'built-in era'. Configs that are hand-written or created by a first write (stampConfigWriteMetadata skips stamping when previousConfig is undefined) never get the marker; worse, stampSkillWorkshopPluginMigration now refuses to stamp on every later ordinary write because this rule always reports a change. So an operator on a current release who intentionally sets plugins.allow: ["telegram"] to harden the install sees a persistent 'needs migration' legacy warning, and openclaw doctor --fix / startup migration silently appends skill-workshop to their allowlist, turning on a plugin that loads learned skills into prompts and runs autonomous learning against their explicit policy. Before this change such a write stamped the marker and left the allowlist alone.

findings.title: Enable button stays stuck on 'Turning on…' when the enable succeeds but Workshop methods never appear
findings.failure: On a successful plugins.setEnabled the owner leaves state at {status:'off', enabling:true} and relies solely on the method catalog gaining skills.workshop.list. If the response reports restartRequired, or the plugin is enabled but fails to load/register its methods, the catalog never changes, sync() is never re-run with a new client, and the page shows a permanently disabled 'Turning on…' button with no error, no retry and no hint that a restart is needed; the result of the request (restartRequired/warnings) is discarded.

findings.title: Model-context reads now rethrow every error, not just bounded-limit rejections
findings.failure: The catch now rethrows any error for view "model-context", not only the new RangeError from the limit. Before this change, ordinary read failures such as SessionTranscriptReadFenceError ("Session transcript changed during context read" when an unadmitted async read races an append), a CodexHistoryRejection for a malformed header, or the 60 s worker timeout returned undefined. Callers then logged a warning and continued with empty or previous history (attempt-context.ts warn branch, run-attempt-context `?? []` and `?? historyState.messages`). Those transient failures now abort the whole Codex attempt during prompt preparation, so the user sees a failed turn where the run used to continue.

findings.title: Compaction hook reads switched to the bounded, throwing model-context view inside event handlers
findings.failure: readMirroredSessionMessages used the native-evidence view, which returned [] on failure. It now uses "model-context", which rethrows. It runs inside handleItemStarted and handleItemCompleted for contextCompaction items, without an admission receipt, while the same run is still checkpointing tool messages into the transcript. A concurrent append makes validateSessionTranscriptContextVersion throw. A newest tool frame larger than the byte budget, which is likely right when Codex compacts a full context, makes the limit throw. Either way the notification handler throws: before/after compaction hooks do not run, and persistCodexContextCompactionActivity and the compaction end event are skipped. Hooks that do run also lose tool-result details and private metadata they used to receive from the native-evidence view.

findings.title: Byte budget counts raw payload bytes such as base64 images against tokens*8, so one large recent message truncates or fails the read
findings.failure: maxBytes is contextTokenBudget*8 (about 1 MB at 128k tokens), measured as octet_length of the projected event JSON. Inline image data and large tool outputs count byte for byte, although they cost few tokens or are sanitized later. The tail scan breaks at the first entry that does not fit instead of skipping it. So one recent 2-4 MB photo or screenshot tool result drops all older history from before_prompt_build hooks and context-engine input, even though the history would easily fit the model's context. If that entry is in the newest message or tool frame, the read throws "cannot fit the model-context limit" and the turn or compaction handling fails until the user runs /reset.

findings.title: Agent owner/creator filters are rejected as 'other people's activity' for session-only callers
findings.failure: ownerId and creatorId are actor-id filters that also match agents (ownerId is the 'assignable owner identity', documented as a configured agent ID for agent owners; creators can be agents). For any caller with a viewer ID (session-only guest, or an agent run started by one), the policy runs every creatorId/ownerId through resolveSessionProfileId and compares it with the viewer's profile ID. An agent ID such as 'main' never matches, so a guest filtering the sidebar by an agent owner, or the sessions_list agent tool called with ownerId/creatorId set to an agent, now gets FORBIDDEN 'Other people's activity is private' even though no person's activity is involved. The owner-facet change (effectiveOwner.identity.id === activityViewerId) also drops agent owners from the facet, so the guest's agent-owner filter options disappear.

findings.title: Guest's saved sidebar owner filter for another person now makes every sidebar list request fail
findings.failure: Before this change guests could pick another person as the sidebar owner filter, and the UI persists that choice in localStorage as 'owner:<id>' (loadStoredSidebarSessionOwnerFilter) and sends it as ownerId on every sidebar sessions.list. After upgrade the Gateway throws FORBIDDEN for that ownerId, so the guest's sidebar session list fails on every load and refresh instead of falling back. The owner facet that would let the UI show and reset the selection comes from the same failing response, and only the Activity page controller was taught to handle the new FORBIDDEN; the sidebar still holds the stale filter.

findings.title: Canvas inventory throws on an unreadable legacy root and aborts the whole recovery capture
findings.failure: collectBackupResources calls listLegacyCanvasDocumentIds, which throws for any non-ENOENT error (EACCES, ENOTDIR) on plugins.entries.canvas.config.host.root/documents. preparePluginDoctorMigrationResources does not catch collector errors, so captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline (and rehearsal plan collection in state-migrations.plugin-doctor.ts) fails outright. Before this change the same config only produced the undeclared-resources warning and detectLegacyState's failure was caught as a 'Failed detecting' warning; now an operator with a stale or permission-restricted retired Canvas root cannot update at all until they fix that directory.

findings.title: Already-migrated host-event archives are declared forever, permanently deferring Memory Core in rehearsal
findings.failure: collectLegacyMemoryHostEventSources returns every events.jsonl.migrated[.N] archive as a ready 'archive' source even after its checkpoint matches and no migration is needed, and the collector declares it unconditionally. Those archives are never deleted, so every later update capture copies them again, and in an update rehearsal whose agent workspace lies outside the rehearsal root (a configured absolute workspace) the path is read-only, so preparePluginDoctorMigrationResources defers the whole memory-core plugin on every update from then on, skipping its sidecar and other migrations in rehearsal with only a 'deferred' notice.

findings.title: Paced live text lags durable history, so duplicate suppression fails and a partial live bubble shows under the recorded answer
findings.failure: liveText() hides the live bubble only when the newest assistant row's raw text exactly equals the live text. The bubble and the shape now feed it displayedStreamingAssistantText, which can trail streamingAssistantText by up to 150 ms, and longer while a touch or scroll keeps the run loop out of default mode. Suppose a history refresh or narration settle records an assistant row with the full text while the run is still live, for example an intermediate item before a tool call, or another client's completion while a local run keeps the stream. If the last delta arrived inside the pacing window, the displayed prefix does not match the durable row. The user then sees the full recorded message plus a truncated duplicate live bubble until the paced flush runs. Before this change the authoritative text matched and the duplicate never showed.

findings.title: Bottom size-change anchor makes user-expanded content near the live edge grow upward
findings.failure: defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom, for: .sizeChanges) applies to every content size change whenever followTarget == .latest and the user is not dragging, not only to the growing live bubble. A reader at the bottom who taps a completed-work disclosure or expands a long user message near the end sees the content above the bottom jump upward. The tapped header can move off the top of the screen and the expanded content grows upward, where before it expanded downward in place.

findings.title: Late signal after a verified successful activation rolls back or fails a healthy update
findings.failure: The in-memory signal phase is only advanced by recordPhase/maybeRestartService and is never cleared once verification succeeds or the run finishes, so it stays 'verifying' for the rest of finalization. If SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP arrives after the new Gateway restarted and passed verification (e.g. during completePostUpdateMaintenance, deferred plugin convergence, or package-completion cleanup), onSignal takes the recovering path and sets admission.interruption. The final `reportResult(await runPostUpdate())` then calls captured.interruptedResult on the 'ok' result, which unconditionally rewrites it to status 'error', reason 'interrupted'; recoverFailedResult then sees an error with a packageTransaction and runs rollbackFailedUpdate, stopping the healthy new Gateway and reverting to the old package (without the DB backup, since gatewayStartAttempted is true). If the signal lands after that first call, line 907 still rewrites the verified 'ok' result to 'error/interrupted'. The operator who closed the SSH session or pressed Ctrl-C after seeing a healthy Gateway gets an unrequested rollback and an extra outage, or a history row/report saying the update failed while the new version is running, prompting an unnecessary 'openclaw update repair'.

findings.title: Interruption overwrites the real failure reason and failed step
findings.failure: recordMutableUpdateInterruption always replaces `reason` with 'interrupted' and `failedStep` with the synthetic signal step whenever the signal step is not already present. When an update has already failed for a real cause (e.g. candidate-verification-failed, restart-unhealthy, a rollback/restore failure) and the signal arrives later, during rollback or cleanup, the second application in finishSettledUpdate (pendingResult at post-update line 907) or the terminal wrapper rewrites the published terminal result so the report and history show 'interrupted' as the reason and the signal step as the failed step. The operator loses the actual root cause of the failed update and the triage/next-action guidance that depends on the original reason.

findings.title: Repeated Ctrl-C/SIGTERM ignored for up to the 30-minute recovery budget
findings.failure: Once the first signal takes the recovering path, the exit gate waits for the whole terminal settlement up to activationTimeoutMs/defaultStepTimeoutMs, which falls back to DEFAULT_UPDATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS (30 minutes) for CLI runs. Any further SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP hits `if (shutdown) return;` and is silently dropped, and the CLI fallback handler has already detached itself. Before this change the first signal exited promptly; now an operator whose rollback or Gateway restart hangs cannot interrupt the updater by pressing Ctrl-C again and has to find and SIGKILL it, which skips the very cleanup this change is meant to guarantee. Even after the budget expires, the exit barrier still awaits in-flight compensations without a bound.

findings.title: New gcp Account variant is treated as an unauthenticated source account in plugin migration
findings.failure: The bumped 0.169.0 protocol adds an Account variant {type: "gcp"} (Vertex AI with external credentials), but readSourceCodexAccount only maps chatgpt/apiKey/amazonBedrock and falls through to "missing" for gcp. A user whose source Codex is authenticated through GCP and who migrates Codex plugins that own apps gets every such plugin blocked with codex_account_unavailable and the message 'Codex app-server did not report an authenticated source account' instead of the codex_subscription_required explanation that other non-ChatGPT accounts get; /codex account likewise shows only 'available'. The CodexGetAccountResponse type in protocol.ts was not extended either.

findings.title: Update preparation now aborts when any plugin's source cannot be statically inspected
findings.failure: prepareUpdateCandidatePlugins now runs inspectPluginSourceDependencies over every enabled plugin entry, setup entry and every declared Doctor contract module (including those of disabled plugins), and nothing catches its errors. inspectPluginSourceDependencies rethrows anything outside a short list of module-not-found codes: parse/lexer failures from visitPluginSourceReferences, 'Plugin source link leaves its package', non-regular build inputs, and so on. The repair path in the same change expects such failures from original sources and turns them into warnings, but this path has no such handling. A user whose custom or npm plugin, or a disabled plugin's doctor-contract file, contains syntax the inspector rejects or a link it refuses could update before this change, because the tree copier just copied the directory. Now the whole update rehearsal fails with an inspection error that is unrelated to the update.

findings.title: Candidate Doctor preflight throws on unparseable copied plugin source even when the snapshot is complete
findings.failure: completeUpdateCandidatePluginRehearsal inspects every selected entry in the private copy, including Doctor contract modules of disabled plugins, with an unguarded inspectPluginSourceDependencies([entry]). Only the later inspection of the original source is wrapped in try/catch. Errors propagate through createDoctorRehearsalSnapshotPreparation into readDoctorConfigPreflightSnapshot, so they fail candidate Doctor preflight. Example: an enabled plugin, or a disabled plugin's doctor-contract module, has a source file the static inspector cannot parse or capture, even though it needs no repair. Every update driven by a published updater then fails in candidate Doctor, where before the plugin was at most reported by Doctor or plugin loading. The 'invalid source' handling only covers the original tree, and the malformed-plugin tests only cover the runtime entries of disabled plugins.

findings.title: Parent counted as running until its own task_notification, so a child forwarded to the main stream after the parent ended can be treated as consumed by the subagent
findings.failure: recordRunningDescendants removes a launcher from the running map only when that launcher's own task_notification arrives. A background_tasks_changed snapshot that no longer lists the launcher does not remove it, and the fixture shows native emits that snapshot before the launcher's notification. Suppose the nested child's task_notification arrives in that window: the launcher has ended (it has left the snapshot), but its notification has not been processed. Native routes the child's completion to the main conversation, yet parentRuns is true. acceptMessage then deletes the child from pendingBackgroundTaskIds and taskNotifications. The next main-stream result is delivered as terminal and the turn completes. The forwarded child answer arrives after the turn has settled, so the user never gets the nested agent's final answer. The remaining entries in runningDescendants can also make completeTurn abort the warm process.

findings.title: Remounted repair bypasses the 'recovery still required' guard and archives unfinished publications unverified
findings.failure: The guard that keeps a pending operation for its recovery owner (assertNoPendingPackageActivation when the live package is still the recorded previous or candidate) compares replacementIdentity against the raw historical descriptor identities, while the rest of the function now uses the device-mapped previousIdentity/candidateIdentity. After a reboot/remount changes device numbers, the live package's identity never equals a raw historical identity, so the guard is skipped. Example: a 'publishing' (or 'publication-complete', or a 'prepared' operation with an armed rollback) journal interrupted while the original package is still installed (replacement == mapped previous): manualReplacement and externalPublication are both false, so `openclaw update repair` falls into the generic settlePackageActivationCustody path and archives the operation as 'recovery-lease-missing'/'superseded-by-manual-install' without restoration or any tree/launcher verification. The settlement-only journal permits this write because the intent is 'settled'. Without remount the same state is refused as needing recovery; with remount, partially rewritten launchers pointing at the (now archived) candidate are left behind and the operator is told the old operation was settled.

findings.title: Drop-tint ::after on the message surface overrides and hides the dictation edge animation in New Session
findings.failure: The New Session message surface is the same element that gets `agent-chat__input--dictating` (composer.tsx:542-545), whose dictation comet is drawn with `.agent-chat__input--dictating::after` (composer.css:87, specificity 0,1,1). The new `.new-session-page__composer > .agent-chat__input::after` rule (specificity 0,2,1) now targets that same pseudo-element and wins every shared property: `opacity: 0`, `background: var(--accent)` instead of the conic gradient, `inset: 0` instead of -1px, `z-index: 1` instead of 5. When a user starts dictation on the New Session page, the travelling accent edge that signals capture is active is invisible (opacity 0). If they then drag a file over the composer while dictating, they see a flat 10% accent ring masked to 1px instead of the drop tint or the comet. Before this change the drop tint lived on the shell's ::after, so the two never collided.

findings.title: Collapsed Subagents avatar stack loses its tinted backgrounds and overlapping glyphs bleed together
findings.failure: The new rule `.chat-details .chat-details-desktop-body .chat-details-subagents__avatar { background: transparent; color: var(--muted) }` (plus adding the avatar to the 16px icon-slot rule) is not scoped to list rows, and at specificity 0,3,0 it beats `.chat-details-subagents__stack > .chat-details-subagents__avatar` (0,2,0). When a session has enough subagents that the Subagents section renders the summary button with the stacked avatars (SubagentAvatar summary, overlapped by margin-inline-start -6px), every stacked avatar becomes a transparent, muted 16px bot glyph with no per-agent hue fill. The overlapping avatars no longer occlude each other, so the user sees a smear of overlapping bot outlines instead of the distinct colored chips. The per-agent hue is also gone from every subagent row.

findings.title: Create PR split button's menu trigger overhangs its pill by 6px
findings.failure: `.chat-details .chat-details-desktop-body .chat-pr__actions-trigger { margin-inline-end: -6px }` also matches the trigger inside `.chat-pr__publication-actions` (the Create PR / menu split button in the Environment branch controls, rendered by ChatBranchActions). That container draws the pill background and rounded corners, and the trigger is its last flex child with no padding after it, so the negative margin pushes the trigger's right 6px outside the pill. With a branch ready to publish, the user sees the menu chevron's button stick out past the shaded split-button background, and the hover/expanded background and right corner radius extend beyond the pill. The branch test now only checks scroll overflow at the scroll port, so it no longer catches this.

findings.title: Capture cleanup failure turns accepted checkpoints into errors and blocks every later checkpoint
findings.failure: removeLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture runs unguarded in the finally block after the guest has resumed and canonical acceptance has finished. It also runs before pausing in prepareLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture, and on the unchanged-probe path in checkpointLocalWorkspace. If removing the snapshot fails, the error replaces the checkpoint's result. Examples: rmSync fails with a code other than EACCES/EPERM/ENOTEMPTY; chmod fails with EPERM on a guest-created directory owned by another UID; the native helper times out or is killed on a very large tree. The command is reported as failed even though its bytes were accepted, and a typed error from run (rejection or conflict) is masked. The leftover checkpoint-capture then makes the leftover removal throw again at the start of every later checkpoint, including unchanged ones. The sandbox cannot checkpoint again until someone removes the directory by hand.

findings.title: Snapshot copy failures no longer fall back to the paused Git capture path
findings.failure: On a btrfs subvolume projection, every changed checkpoint now depends on the native copy subprocess. Only errors coded CLONE_UNAVAILABLE, EXDEV or ENOSYS fall back to run(). Other failures make the whole checkpoint throw instead of using the existing paused Git capture, which would have succeeded. Examples are the generic "Native worktree copy failed: <termination>" errors from write() (timeout, killed, process-tree-extinction failure), EPERM/EACCES from snapshot creation, and ENOSPC. Each mutating command's finalization then fails, and keeps failing while the condition lasts. Before this change these checkpoints did not depend on the native helper at all.

findings.title: Tool disclosures lose their touch hit area
findings.failure: On a coarse-pointer device, expanded activity groups render each tool disclosure with zero vertical padding; the only coarse-pointer rule restores padding for activity-group summaries, not tool rows. Each toggle therefore shrinks to roughly the 19.5px text line height, down from the previous padded row, making dense adjacent tool rows substantially easier to mistap.

findings.title: Completed bubble activity collapses to a tiny toggle
findings.failure: In bubble mode, an activity disclosure has a 40px target while it is working, but once the run completes and the `chat-activity-group--working` class is removed, this rule leaves it with zero padding and no minimum height. The completed activity toggle becomes only about one 13px text line tall on touch screens, instead of retaining the previous 28px minimum, so users get a difficult-to-tap control for reopening completed details.

findings.title: Sterile probe rejects version-manager Node shims
findings.failure: When a Bun-hosted gateway has a compatible Node available only through a PATH shim or wrapper that needs HOME, PATH, ASDF_DATA_DIR, VOLTA_HOME, or similar environment state, the almost-empty probe environment makes that shim fail. The resolver then reports no compatible Node, so requested Tool Search code mode silently falls back to structured tools even though a valid Node installation is available.

findings.title: Cancellation cannot interrupt deferred skill preparation
findings.failure: If skill-library session creation or authoring stalls after the send is acknowledged, `chat.abort` marks the run canceled but cannot interrupt either await. The canceled run retains its reply-admission ticket until preparation eventually returns, so later sends to the session can receive `status: "started"` yet remain blocked indefinitely behind work the user already canceled.

findings.title: Overlapping footer blocks interaction with visible transcript content
findings.failure: After scrolling a message link or selectable text into the new 28–35px overlap band, it remains visible beside the composer's rounded corners, but the full-width `.chat-footer` box is painted above the transcript and receives pointer/touch hit-testing across that entire band. Clicking the exposed link or starting a mobile selection/swipe there targets the footer instead of the message, leaving visibly exposed transcript content non-interactive.

findings.title: Finalizer bounds storage-only tool details as model input
findings.failure: When the completed current-turn tool result carries large or non-JSON-serializable `details` (for example aggregated process output), sizing serializes those details before `sanitizeSessionHistory` strips them from model context. The selector can therefore discard usable history, throw the context-limit error, or fail during JSON serialization, leaving the user without the final answer even though the actual provider input would fit.

findings.title: Rebounding loses the mandatory compaction summary
findings.failure: Every frozen message is represented as an ordinary `message`, including a `compactionSummary` that came from the transcript's mandatory compaction boundary. If the snapshot contains that summary, a retained old turn, and a new completed tool turn that pushes the snapshot over the limit, suffix selection drops the old turn together with the summary. The finalizer then answers without the only surviving summary of earlier instructions, even though the canonical selector would keep the boundary while dropping only the retained turn.

findings.title: Popup cap hides full dashboard author names
findings.failure: In a browser supporting `appearance: base-select`, open the dashboard Author filter when owner labels are longer than 320px (especially labels sharing the same prefix). The new 320px popup cap and single-line option clipping truncate those labels, while the raw dashboard `<option>` elements have no `title`; users can see identical ellipsized entries and cannot determine which author they are selecting. Previously the picker could expand nearly to the viewport and the options were not forcibly clipped.

findings.title: Spawned dashboard runs lose restart recovery
findings.failure: When an interactive dashboard session originally created via `sessions_spawn` is executing a later user/operator turn during shutdown, its key is not a subagent-shaped key, so `resolveRootSubagentRequester` does not redirect it to its requester. This new `createdVia === "spawn"` check then excludes the session itself from restart marking. Shutdown aborts the turn, but neither the child nor its requester receives a restart-resume input, leaving the interrupted work unreconciled after startup.

findings.title: Snapshot copies reject aliased staging roots
findings.failure: When the snapshot staging path has a non-native spelling—such as a Windows LOCALAPPDATA/XDG_CACHE_HOME using an 8.3 path, or a POSIX staging root beneath a symlink ancestor—the code passes that spelling directly as copyRootFileSync's destination root. fs-safe requires roots to match their native realpath (the repository already rebases such roots in plugin-source-file.ts), so the guarded copy throws a path-mismatch error. Doctor/update state inspection then aborts even though the configured cache directory is writable; the previous descriptor-based copier accepted these paths.

findings.title: Channel authorization URLs are fetched on hover
findings.failure: Channel setup uses the same WizardStep.externalUrl mechanism for provider OAuth URLs (including state/query credentials), but this anchor lacks data-link-reader-external. Hovering or keyboard-focusing it now calls controlUi.linkPreview and makes an anonymous GET to the authorization URL before the user chooses to open it, potentially leaking or consuming a signed/one-time flow. Only the model wizard's equivalent link was excluded.

findings.title: Base refresh can race Review and return a stale diff
findings.failure: If Review reads accepted base A, then a concurrent base refresh advances the projection to B while the request waits for the Git read, the returned guard does not detect it: it watches only session state and registry identity/removal, not the projection revision or base_commit. The Git read can therefore compare the refreshed checkout against A, so the user sees newly accepted upstream changes as task changes and incorrect branch history even though the refresh completed before the response.

findings.title: Excluded plugins survive in legacy profile paths
findings.failure: For a valid manifest using the supported legacy `metadata.openclaw.config: profiles/custom.yaml`, unchecking a plugin removes its `packages` entry but rewrites extensions only when the file path is exactly `profiles/openclaw.yml`. The custom profile remains in the archive with that plugin extension, so installing the published Claw still installs/enables the plugin the creator excluded.

findings.title: Excluding a managed avatar makes the draft invalid
findings.failure: If `agent.identity.avatar` names a destination in `workspace.files`, unchecking that source removes the workspace entry but leaves the avatar reference. Manifest validation then rejects the rebuilt package because a local avatar must match a managed destination, so the creator cannot review or publish the Claw without the optional avatar.

findings.title: Publication uses a Gateway-wide account rather than the acting creator
findings.failure: On a multi-user Gateway, an administrator publishing from their Control UI does not supply or bind a ClawHub credential to their authenticated user profile. The code loads the process-wide environment/CLI token, so if the Gateway host was logged into ClawHub as another person, the administrator's publish action uploads under that other person's account.

findings.title: Interrupted refresh can discard its accepted base
findings.failure: The binding is updated by accept() before MERGE_HEAD is written. If the operation is interrupted in that window and the PR is then retargeted to an unrelated branch, the retry sees no pending MERGE_HEAD and replaces previous.base with the new GitHub target. It therefore integrates the new target and never finishes the already accepted base, contrary to the documented recovery behavior.

findings.title: Previously marked allowlists are never repaired
findings.failure: If an earlier version already recorded meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin=true while leaving plugins.allow without skill-workshop—as the previous migration or an ordinary config write could do—Doctor returns at the marker guard before reaching this new allowlist repair. Upgrading and running doctor --fix therefore leaves Workshop disabled for exactly those previously migrated operators.

findings.title: The enable button is offered when policy makes enabling impossible
findings.failure: With plugins.enabled:false or plugins.deny containing skill-workshop, plugins.list reports the installed plugin as disabled, so the page classifies it as "off" and offers Turn on Skill Workshop. plugins.setEnabled refuses these configurations as "plugins disabled" or "blocked by denylist", leaving the operator with a button that can never turn Workshop on.

findings.title: A failed plugin activation leaves the page permanently enabling
findings.failure: When enabling persists successfully but the plugin fails to load (for example because a runtime dependency is missing), plugins.setEnabled can resolve while the refreshed method catalog still lacks skills.workshop.list. The ensuing same-client capability update calls sync with the existing client, which returns without re-reading plugins.list, so the UI remains stuck on the disabled "Turning on…" button instead of switching to the enabled-but-failed message.

findings.title: State metadata bypasses bounded-context limits
findings.failure: A transcript can contain an older `model_change` or `thinking_level_change` with an arbitrarily large string (the public append methods impose no maximum), followed by a small latest message. A bounded `openModelContext` read selects the message within `maxBytes`, then reinserts the unmeasured metadata entry here. The returned context—and an async worker transfer—can therefore exceed `maxBytes` by an arbitrary amount, defeating the memory bound the new API and Codex hook path rely on.

findings.title: Session-only callers cannot filter shared sessions by agent owner or creator
findings.failure: For a session-only caller, any creatorId or ownerId unequal to the caller's profile ID is treated as another person's profile. However, these fields accept general actor identities, including agents. Requesting sessions.list with ownerId or creatorId such as "main" for an otherwise visible shared, agent-owned session now returns FORBIDDEN instead of that session, even though no person's private activity was requested.

findings.title: Canonical legacy path aborts the entire recovery capture
findings.failure: If an agent's legacy memory-search store path is the canonical per-agent database path itself, collectLegacyMemorySidecarSources retains it because isCanonicalAgentDatabaseSymlink only excludes symlinks. The collector then declares that same absolute path first as `sqlite` here and again as `file` at line 504. preparePluginDoctorMigrationResources rejects the conflicting kinds, so the updater logs that original-state capture is unavailable and continues without any recovery copy; standalone Doctor likewise continues after the capture failure. Thus all migrations in that run, including Canvas and host-event moves, proceed without the recovery evidence this change is intended to guarantee.

findings.title: Late SQLite companions are moved without being inventoried
findings.failure: The collector declares legacy `-wal`, `-shm`, and `-journal` paths and their archive destinations only when they exist during collection. If a companion is created after the recovery capture is sealed but before migration—such as by the still-running legacy SQLite user, or a `-shm` created when the importer attaches a WAL database—archiveLegacyMemorySidecar later re-enumerates it and renames it to `<path>.migrated`. Neither that companion nor its destination is present in the recovery manifest, so rollback cannot restore its bytes or remove the newly created archive. All possible suffix paths and destinations need missing entries just as the retry destinations do.

findings.title: Signal recovery loses its admission at mutation start
findings.failure: Every real mutable update calls `deferLedgerWrites()` at mutation start, which removes the run from `admissions`. Subsequent restart/verification scopes therefore take this no-admission path, phase updates and interruption recording also become no-ops, and compensation is not registered. If SIGTERM/SIGHUP arrives while restarting or verifying, forward work is not cancelled and the terminal report can remain successful or omit the interruption (the immediate message can also incorrectly say `activating`), rather than reporting the signal and stopping forward work as promised.

findings.title: Realpathing file locators loses the configured plugin ID
findings.failure: For a manifestless file plugin loaded through an in-directory symlink such as `my-id.ts -> implementation.ts`, with `plugins.allow: ["my-id"]`, discovery normally identifies the plugin as `my-id`. This code instead discovers the real target, identifies it as `implementation`, and treats it as disabled, so its sibling imports outside the containing directory are omitted from the snapshot. Candidate Doctor/runtime then fails with a module-not-found error even though the enabled source plugin works.

findings.title: Foreground descendant can terminate the outer turn
findings.failure: When a foreground Agent launches a background child, the parent finishes, and the child’s forwarded notification result arrives before the main query’s final result, the child is now owned by the current input even though it was deliberately excluded from pendingBackgroundTaskIds. Its notification is queued and its task-origin result is therefore treated as the current input’s terminal answer. The iterator closes with the child answer and the foreground parent’s actual final answer is dropped; this is the reverse completion order of the existing foreground-descendant test, which only covers the parent result arriving while the child still runs.

findings.title: Remapped previous package bypasses inconsistent-publication refusal
findings.failure: After device numbers change, consider a `publication-complete` journal whose live installation is the recorded previous package and whose recovery lease is still current. `replacementIdentity` equals the projected `previousIdentity`, but cannot equal either raw historical identity. The final `includes(replacementIdentity)` guard is therefore false, so repair skips the refusal and archives the operation as `superseded-by-manual-install` without verifying a newer installation. The operator is told recovery is closed and subsequent updates are admitted even though the supposedly published candidate disappeared while its original owner remained valid.

findings.title: In-place manual upgrades are mistaken for the old candidate
findings.failure: If an operator installs a newer OpenClaw version by replacing files inside the existing package directory, the directory retains the remount-projected candidate inode. Repair classifies it as `externalPublication` solely from that identity, then verifies it against the old candidate's full digest. The legitimate newer contents fail with `Package settlement full candidate fingerprint changed`, so the advertised manual-upgrade recovery remains blocked unless the installer happened to replace the package directory inode.

findings.title: Newer installations are checked against the obsolete launcher
findings.failure: For a remounted journal replaced by a newer manual installation, this calls `verifyPackagePublicationSettlement` with the old descriptor's `launchers`. That verifier compares each live launcher to `entry.candidate`, which describes the interrupted older candidate, not the newer package's manifest/bin target. A valid newer release or package-manager installation that changes its launcher target or wrapper is rejected with `Package settlement launcher changed`, despite its manifest and inventories being valid.

findings.title: Drop overlay replaces the active-dictation indicator
findings.failure: When a user starts voice dictation on the New Session page, the input has `agent-chat__input--dictating`, whose `::after` draws the animated dictation edge. This new rule targets the same pseudo-element with higher specificity and always sets its opacity to 0 while replacing its gradient and geometry, so the dictation edge disappears even when no file is being dragged.

findings.title: Task progress content is no longer vertically centered
findings.failure: For any one-line desktop task-progress step, the plan still overrides `--details-row-padding-block` to 2px and the grid uses `align-items: start`, but this rule increases the minimum row height from 24px to 30px. The 20px marker and text therefore remain pinned 2px from the top with 8px below them, so task rows appear visibly top-heavy instead of sharing the centered 30px alignment of the other Details rows.

findings.title: Aggregate subagent avatars lose their identity colors
findings.failure: When a desktop session has more than five subagents, the aggregate row renders a stack of hue-coded `.chat-details-subagents__avatar` elements. This higher-specificity rule makes every avatar transparent and muted, overriding the stack's per-subagent hashed background colors, so all agents appear as indistinguishable gray bot icons rather than the colored identity stack supplied by the component.

findings.title: Handoff disclosure arrows become permanently invisible
findings.failure: When a run waits on multiple subagents or displays a resumed handoff with session details, its disclosure uses chat-tool-row__chevron inside chat-subagent-wait__toggle or chat-handoff-resume__rule. The new opacity: 0 hides these arrows, but neither control matches the rules that restore visibility. The arrows remain invisible on hover, keyboard focus, and expansion, leaving users without the visual indication that the session lists can be expanded or collapsed.

findings.title: Cancelled preparation keeps later sends blocked
findings.failure: If skill selection or authoring preparation stalls, the user can successfully abort the acknowledged run, but its admission ticket remains held until preparation returns. Neither preparation await observes the abort signal, and the ticket is released only when dispatch settles. A subsequent message in the same session therefore waits behind the cancelled run, even if its own preparation completes. Stop cannot unblock the conversation while the original preparation remains stalled.

findings.title: Strip tool-result metadata before applying the context byte limit
findings.failure: Settled snapshots retain tool-result `details`, but this sizing callback counts them, and the omission projection only replaces `content`. A tool returning small model-facing content with metadata larger than the context byte limit therefore causes the selector to discard its completed tool evidence or throw before finalization. The user gets a final answer without the operation's result, or failed finalization. Previously, transcript hydration stripped `details` before sizing; ordinary model requests also strip them. Apply that same projection before bounding the snapshot.

findings.title: Failure-notice retries are rejected after the lifecycle write succeeds
findings.failure: For a batch with requesterRunId, a permanent handoff failure first commits the requester's failed lifecycle, then appends its transcript notice in persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent. If that append fails transiently, settlement retries this call with requireYielded: true. The requester now has status "failed", so the lifecycle projection rejects the retry and never retries the notice append. Settlement then releases the batch, leaving the conversation without the promised delivery-failure explanation and recovery guidance.

findings.title: Creating a sandbox hides task commits made before sandbox creation
findings.failure: If a session commits task changes while sandboxing is off, then enables a local sandbox, projectionOperations.prepare initializes the new projection's base_commit to the checkout's current HEAD. This change unconditionally uses that value as Review's base, even though no upstream refresh occurred. Previously visible task changes disappear from All changes, their commits disappear from branch history, and selecting those commits returns unknown_commit. The projection's initial checkout revision is not necessarily the task's upstream base.

findings.title: Profile plugin dependencies are absent from review selections
findings.failure: When a proposal declares plugins in profiles/openclaw.yml's extensions array, the review lists no plugin items for those dependencies because it enumerates only manifest.packages. Their exclusion IDs are rejected as unknown, and publication retains the extensions. Consumers subsequently install those dependencies through planClawExtensions. The creator cannot remove an individual profile plugin while retaining the profile's other settings.

findings.title: Excluding the avatar file leaves an invalid manifest
findings.failure: For a draft with agent.identity.avatar referencing a managed workspace image, excluding that image removes its workspace.files entry but preserves the avatar reference. The subsequent build fails manifest validation because the avatar must match a workspace.files destination. Consequently, unchecking this optional file prevents review and publication instead of producing a package without the avatar.

findings.title: New explicit Workshop disables can be erased by Doctor
findings.failure: With an unmarked config containing plugins.allow: ["diffs"] and no Workshop entry, an ordinary config write adding plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled: false now produces an allowlist migration change. Consequently, stampSkillWorkshopPluginMigration leaves the config unmarked. The write-refusal guard allows this write because the previous config has no ignored entry or deny rule. On the next Doctor repair, the newly authored disable is treated as historical policy and deleted, and Workshop is added to the allowlist. Workshop then runs despite the operator's explicit disable. Previously this write recorded the marker and preserved the disable.

findings.title: Respect read-only plugin inventory before offering enablement
findings.failure: When Workshop is disabled on a Gateway using OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1 or OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1, plugins.list returns mutationAllowed: false. This code discards that flag, so an admin still sees an active Turn on Skill Workshop button. Every click is rejected by the plugin mutation service; the page offers an operation that cannot work instead of explaining that configuration must be changed through its external owner.

findings.title: Git rollback inherits the cancelled forward scope
findings.failure: The new forward scope encloses all of updateGitInstall, including updateGitCheckout's internal rollbackError/restoreRuntime recovery. If a signal arrives after checkout mutation starts but before the retained transaction is registered, stopping this scope also cancels recovery: runGitRollbackSteps cannot launch its reset/checkout commands because spawnCommandWithInvocation rejects the aborted scope. The updater therefore leaves the checkout unrestored and the Gateway stopped even when the previous runtime is available. Internal Git rollback must execute outside the cancelled forward scope.

findings.title: Missing bare-package imports never trigger snapshot repair
findings.failure: A custom plugin can import a hoisted workspace package that is installed in an ancestor node_modules directory but not declared in the plugin's own manifest. The published updater omits that dependency. In the copied snapshot, captureModule returns undefined for the missing bare-package import, but this condition records only relative or absolute imports as unresolved. completeUpdateCandidatePluginRehearsal therefore treats the snapshot as complete and skips recovery, even when the original package is available and unchanged. Candidate Doctor or the canary subsequently fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

findings.title: Published launcher inodes are rejected during remount settlement
findings.failure: If publication replaced a launcher before the reboot, the newly supported publishing/publication-complete settlement path rejects the intact installation. Publication copies the launcher into a fresh inode and records that identity in publications (or the pending launcher intent). inspectRemountedPackagePublication instead compares against the previous launcher inode or the staged candidate launcher inode, ignoring those recorded publication identities. Repair therefore throws "Package settlement inode or device mapping changed" and leaves subsequent updates blocked despite an unchanged, successfully published candidate.

findings.title: Drop overlay hides the active dictation indicator
findings.failure: When a user starts dictation in New Session, the composer receives agent-chat__input--dictating, whose ::after renders the animated recording border. The new, more specific selector targets that same pseudo-element, replacing its gradient and setting opacity to 0 whenever no file is being dragged. The recording border therefore disappears during normal dictation. During a simultaneous file drag, the retained dictation mask also prevents the intended full-surface drop tint.

findings.title: Keep handoff disclosure arrows visible
findings.failure: ChatSubagentWaitLine and ChatHandoffResume also use .chat-tool-row__chevron, but their buttons lack .chat-inline-disclosure. Setting the shared class to opacity: 0 hides their arrows permanently: none of the reveal selectors match on hover, keyboard focus, or expansion. Users see waiting/resume text without the disclosure indicator that makes the session list discoverable or indicates its expanded state.

findings.title: Cached Node path becomes unusable after a Homebrew upgrade
findings.failure: Under Bun, probing /opt/homebrew/bin/node returns Node's resolved process.execPath in a versioned Homebrew Cellar directory. This path is cached indefinitely. When Homebrew upgrades Node and removes that directory, PATH remains unchanged, so the resolver keeps returning the deleted executable. Tool Search continues advertising code mode, but every invocation fails with ENOENT until OpenClaw restarts.

findings.title: Probe drops environment needed by Node version managers
findings.failure: If a Bun-hosted installation's only compatible Node is exposed through a version-manager shim using a custom VOLTA_HOME or ASDF_DATA_DIR, the probe removes those variables and HOME. The shim cannot locate the installed Node, and the system-location fallbacks find nothing. OpenClaw then silently falls back to structured tools despite a compatible Node being installed and available through the operator's PATH.

findings.title: Node discovery now drops environment required by existing installations
findings.failure: When running tests under Bun with Node installed through an asdf installation that requires a custom ASDF_DATA_DIR, delegating to the new resolver removes that variable from the discovery subprocess. The asdf node shim can no longer find the installed Node version. If no system Node is available, resolveTestNodeExecPath throws "Unable to locate a Node executable" and subprocess-based tests fail despite a working Node on PATH. The previous probe inherited the environment and supported this setup.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve interaction with messages visible through the overlap
findings.failure: When a user scrolls a message into the new overlap, text and links remain visible beside the composer's rounded corners and in its side gutters. The positioned, full-width .chat-footer now covers that strip and retains pointer-events: auto, so clicks and selection attempts hit the transparent footer instead of the visible message. On touch devices, swipes starting there also miss the transcript scrollport.

findings.title: Preserve compaction boundaries when bounding the settled view
findings.failure: Every snapshot item is wrapped as a normal message, including compactionSummary messages. selectBoundedModelRequests protects summaries only when their entry type is compaction. Consequently, when a compacted session's settled snapshot exceeds the byte or event limit—even after tool-result omission—the suffix selection can silently discard its compaction summary. Previously, transcript hydration reserved that boundary and retained it alongside the bounded suffix. The finalizer can now answer a follow-up using tool receipts without the summarized requirements or decisions needed to interpret them, producing an incorrect final answer.

findings.title: Truncation hides the distinction between media devices
findings.failure: In browsers supporting base-select, opening the microphone or camera picker in Settings now truncates long device names to one line. MediaDeviceField renders raw options without title attributes, so devices whose labels share a long prefix but differ at the end appear identical, with no way to reveal the distinguishing suffix visually. Previously the popup could grow or wrap to display those names. Preserve a way to inspect full labels before choosing a device.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the notice receipt when lifecycle settlement partially succeeds
findings.failure: After a permanently rejected child handoff, persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent commits the requester's failed status before separately appending the failure notice. If that append encounters a transient storage failure, settlement retries this call, but requireYielded now rejects the already-failed session. The retry returns successfully and releases the batch without ever recording the notice. The user loses the explanation and instructions for recovering saved child work. Retain and retry the notice append independently once the lifecycle write commits.

findings.title: [P2] Route spawned dashboard children to their requester before skipping them
findings.failure: When an executing child has a dashboard key and createdVia:"spawn", shutdown now skips it. However, resolveRootSubagentRequester only follows ancestry for subagent-shaped keys, so neither the active-run enumeration nor listLiveSubagentRootSessions redirects this child to its requester. If the requester has already finished its turn and has no yield batch, it receives no restart marker. Restart stops the child, and neither conversation receives recovery input, leaving the delegated work abandoned.

findings.title: [P2] Continue queued inputs when recording a lost-source failure fails
findings.failure: For an unreachable yield with accepted queued messages, resumeAfterRestart is cleared before recordRestartYieldFailure runs. If that call throws, for example because the failure notice cannot be appended, control jumps to the outer catch and skips continueSessionQueuedInputs. The accepted messages remain stranded, and the next startup cancels them as orphaned inputs because their preserving marker has already been removed. The ordinary resume-failure path catches notice errors specifically so those messages can still continue.

findings.title: [P2] First sandbox use hides earlier task commits from Review
findings.failure: A session can make and commit task changes while running without a sandbox, then enable sandbox execution in the same managed worktree. When the projection is first created, local-workspace-state.ts initializes base_commit from the current HEAD, including those task commits. Returning that value unconditionally as the Review base makes the earlier changes disappear from All changes and branch history; requesting those commits individually returns unknown_commit. Previously, Review compared against the branch merge base and retained those changes. The projection's initial checkout HEAD must be distinguished from an accepted upstream base before using it for task Review.

findings.title: Spinner disappears inside the pending-agent status wrapper
findings.failure: While an agent is being created, app-sidebar-agent-menu.tsx renders .btn__spinner inside a plain status span. The spinner remains an empty inline element, so its width and height do not apply. Removing its border collapses its painted width to zero, making the pending indicator disappear. Set an explicit display such as inline-block so the mask has a sized box outside flex/grid layouts.

findings.title: [P2] Allow exclusions for every item returned by review
findings.failure: A valid draft can declare more than 128 optional dependencies because manifest packages, MCP servers, and cron jobs have no corresponding count limit. Reviewing a draft with 129 MCP declarations succeeds and returns 129 selectable items, but excluding all of them makes both review and publish fail with INVALID_REQUEST because excluded exceeds maxItems: 128. Creators cannot apply their selections without manually editing the proposal; successive reviews do not help because exclusions are not persisted.

findings.title: Profile extension dependencies cannot be individually excluded
findings.failure: A valid draft can declare plugins solely in profiles/openclaw.yml's extensions array. Only manifest.packages entries become plugin review items, so these dependencies have no checkbox, and submitting their package IDs as exclusions fails with invalid_review_choices. The creator must remove the entire profile, including unrelated agent settings, to omit one such plugin; otherwise the published Claw still requires its installation.

findings.title: Removing a profile leaves its explicit manifest pointer dangling
findings.failure: For a supported draft with metadata.openclaw.config set to profiles/openclaw.yml, unchecking that file removes its contents but preserves the metadata pointer. The subsequent package build tries to read the deleted profile and fails with openclaw_profile_read_failed, preventing the creator from reviewing or publishing that selection.

findings.title: Preserve newly written Workshop policy while allowlist migration is pending
findings.failure: With an unmarked config containing plugins.allow: ["diffs"] and no Workshop entry, an operator can save plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled: false. The write-refusal helper permits this, but the new allowlist change makes stampSkillWorkshopPluginMigration withhold the migration marker. Runtime reads consequently ignore the newly saved entry, and a later doctor --fix deletes it as stale and adds Workshop to the allowlist, turning Workshop on despite the explicit disable. Previously this write stamped the marker and preserved the disable.

findings.title: Refresh availability when plugin state changes on the same connection
findings.failure: Open Workshop while its plugin is enabled but failed to load, then disable the plugin from another client. Both method catalogs lack skills.workshop.list, so sync receives the same client and skips the inventory check. The page keeps saying the plugin failed to load and never offers Turn on Skill Workshop until the page is reopened or the connection changes.

findings.title: Respect the catalog's mutationAllowed flag
findings.failure: On a Gateway running with OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1 or OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1 and Workshop disabled, plugins.list returns mutationAllowed:false. This code discards that flag and exposes the enable button to admins. Every click fails because the backend forbids configuration writes, leaving operators with an action that cannot work instead of explaining that changes are disabled.

findings.title: Respect read-only configuration before offering plugin enablement
findings.failure: With Workshop disabled and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1 or OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1, an admin still sees an active “Turn on Skill Workshop” button because this condition checks only method availability and admin scope. plugins.list explicitly reports mutationAllowed=false in these setups, and plugins.setEnabled always rejects the operation.
