The page therefore offers a recovery action that cannot succeed instead of explaining that the externally managed configuration must be changed.

findings.title: History read failures suppress native compaction completion
findings.failure: Switching to model-context makes history read errors propagate. For example, a transcript checkpoint appended while the asynchronous read is in progress causes snapshot validation to reject. During a contextCompaction completion notification, this exits handleItemCompleted before persisting the compaction activity or emitting the compaction end event. The notification controller only logs the exception at debug level, so a successful native compaction silently loses its history marker and can leave consumers waiting for the end event.

findings.title: Agent owner and creator filters are rejected as foreign people
findings.failure: For a session-only guest, sessions.list with ownerId or creatorId set to a configured agent ID (for example, "research") now throws FORBIDDEN because that ID differs from the guest's profile ID. These are actor filters that also support agents, so guests can no longer filter otherwise readable shared sessions by their agent owner or creator; they instead receive the misleading "Other people's activity is private" error.

findings.title: [P1] Empty legacy .sqlite placeholders abort recovery capture
findings.failure: When a configured external legacy sidecar ends in `.sqlite` and is empty or malformed, declaring it as `file` still sends it through SQLite snapshotting: `isSqliteSnapshotFile` unconditionally accepts the `.sqlite` suffix. Recovery capture then calls `createVerifiedSqliteSnapshot` with `requireNonEmptySource: true`, which rejects an empty placeholder (and malformed databases also fail). Consequently, an update requiring recovery capture aborts before the migration can remove the harmless empty placeholder. The collector's intended header-based classification does not occur for these filenames.

findings.title: Suppress recorded replies using authoritative stream text
findings.failure: If "Hello" is displayed, "Hello world" arrives and is queued, and a narration or session-message event records "Hello world" before the paced flush, this projection compares history against the stale "Hello". The transcript consequently shows both the recorded reply and an extra partial reply. Previously, comparison against streamingAssistantText suppressed that duplicate immediately. It now remains until the flush, potentially throughout touch scrolling because publication waits for the default run-loop mode.

findings.title: Cancellation also closes the Git rollback command scope
findings.failure: If SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP arrives after Git checkout mutation starts but before onTransaction registers the retained transaction, cancellation closes the scope enclosing updateGitInstall. Its immediate rollback also runs inside that scope: runGitRollbackSteps cannot spawn its git reset/checkout commands because spawnCommand rejects with "Command process scope is closed". The checkout can remain partially updated and the Gateway stopped, with no retained transaction available to finish restoration. Immediate rollback needs to execute outside the canceled forward scope.

findings.title: The staged package operation does not inherit cancellation
findings.failure: For the default package candidate-admission path, stagePackageInstallUpdate starts runPackageInstallUpdate before this scope exists. stagedPackage.run only resolves its continuation and awaits the existing operation; AsyncLocalStorage does not move that operation into the caller's scope. Consequently, a signal during its activation Doctor does not cancel that child. If the Doctor hangs beyond the signal recovery budget, the updater exits before rollback and restart, leaving the Gateway stopped despite announcing recovery.

findings.title: Cancellation also disables immediate Git rollback
findings.failure: The new scope wraps all of updateGitInstall, including its internal rollbackError/restoreRuntime recovery. If SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP arrives during Git checkout, after the Gateway stops but before onTransaction publishes a retained transaction, stop() aborts this scope. The subsequent Git rollback commands inherit the aborted signal and cannot execute. The outer finalizer has no retained transaction to retry restoration, leaving the Gateway stopped and potentially leaving a partially changed checkout despite announcing recovery before exit.

findings.title: Missing bare imports are omitted from repair discovery
findings.failure: When a published-driver snapshot lacks a hoisted package imported by name, captureModule returns undefined because that package cannot be found in the private tree. Since local is false, the inspector records no unresolved reference. completeUpdateCandidatePluginRehearsal consequently skips recovery even when the original package remains available, and candidate validation still fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. This occurs with custom plugins using an ancestor's node_modules dependency without declaring it in their own manifest.

findings.title: Sibling modules lose their explicitly referenced assets
findings.failure: If a plugin imports ../shared/helper.js and that helper reads new URL('./data.json', import.meta.url), the inspector captures helper.js but discards its asset reference. External helpers are captured selectively, so data.json never enters the copy plan. The private snapshot then fails with ENOENT when the helper reads the asset, despite both files being available in the original tree.

findings.title: [P2] Honor recorded launcher identities when settling remounted publications
findings.failure: The expanded inspection now accepts publication-complete records and partially acknowledged publications, but its launcher loop still checks only previousIdentity or candidateIdentity. When publication replaces a launcher, copyPackagePathEntry creates a new inode, recorded in record.publications or the pending launcher intent; candidateIdentity identifies the retained source instead. After a reboot remaps devices, repair therefore rejects this valid installed candidate with 'Package settlement inode or device mapping changed' and leaves updates blocked. Settlement must use the recorded published launcher identity for these newly supported states.

findings.title: Remounted repair rejects normally published launchers
findings.failure: If publication finishes but the process stops before retirement, then a reboot changes device numbers, repair reaches this remount inspection with a publication-complete journal. Normal publication copies each launcher into a new inode recorded in initial.publications. The inspector instead checks against the original launcher inode or the staged launcher asset's inode, ignoring those publication records. It throws "Package settlement inode or device mapping changed" even when the installed candidate and launchers are intact, leaving repair and subsequent updates blocked.

findings.title: Preserve the dictation indicator when adding the drop overlay
findings.failure: Starting voice dictation in New Session adds `agent-chat__input--dictating`, whose animated recording border already uses `::after` in chat/composer.css. This new, more specific selector overrides that same pseudo-element's background and sets its opacity to zero. Users therefore lose the animated recording indicator throughout dictation, even without dragging a file.

findings.title: Preserve Podman's environment when selecting the native fixture store
findings.failure: When an operator supplies the required private Podman store through CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF, the earlier createGatewayBenchEnv assignment removes that variable from process.env. These new Podman calls consequently use a different store: image inspection fails even though the specified image exists in the private store, and the benchmark exits before measuring anything. Preserve the Podman environment consistently for fixture creation, checkpoint engine calls, and cleanup.

findings.title: Detect mounted directories before accepting a btrfs snapshot
findings.failure: If an operator mounts another filesystem or bind-mounts a directory beneath the btrfs workspace, the snapshot contains the underlying mountpoint directory rather than the mounted contents. That directory has an ordinary inode, so the inode-2 completeness check does not trigger fallback. Checkpointing can therefore succeed while omitting new files or propagating deletions of previously accepted files beneath the mount into the canonical workspace. The previous live-tree capture included those files.

findings.title: Sterile probes cannot resolve version-manager Node shims
findings.failure: When Bun runs with Node installed through asdf using a custom ASDF_DATA_DIR, and only the asdf shims directory is on PATH, the probe removes ASDF_DATA_DIR, HOME, and PATH before executing the shim. The shim cannot locate its installed Node, so the resolver rejects an otherwise compatible installation and Tool Search falls back to structured tools. The shared test resolver also now throws in this setup, whereas its previous probe inherited the environment and resolved Node successfully.

findings.title: [P2] Exclude tool-result metadata before applying the byte limit
findings.failure: Settled snapshots retain newly completed tools' `details`, but this sizing callback counts those storage-only fields before `sanitizeSessionHistory` removes them. A tool returning a short receipt with sufficiently large metadata can therefore exceed the finalizer's byte limit even though its model-visible content fits. The omission projection also retains `details`, so the selector can discard the completed tool frame or reject finalization altogether. Previously, transcript hydration stripped these fields before bounding. Users consequently lose the final summary or receive an answer without the completed operation's evidence.

findings.title: Failure-notice retries silently lose the notice after terminal settlement
findings.failure: When a completion handoff permanently fails, persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent first commits the requester's failed lifecycle, then separately appends the transcript failure notice. If that append fails temporarily, settlement retains a retry. However, the retry repeats the lifecycle event with requireYielded:true; the already-failed session now fails that predicate, so the helper returns without retrying the notice. Settlement then clears its pending receipt. The user permanently loses the classified delivery-failure notice and its recovery guidance, even after storage recovers.

findings.title: Canonicalize the destination root before guarded copying
findings.failure: On Windows, a stagingRoot containing an 8.3 directory alias creates targetPath with that alias still present. copyRootFileSync compares ordinary and native root spellings and rejects this as a moved root—the same limitation handled by resolveNativeCopySource in src/plugins/plugin-source-file.ts. Consequently, synchronous artifact-preserving inspection fails with a path-mismatch error on an otherwise writable staging directory, whereas the previous descriptor copier succeeded. The destination directory and target path need rebasing onto the native realpath before admission.

findings.title: Shadow DOM link previews miss pointer transitions
findings.failure: In a rendered Markdown skill preview, links live inside the file-preview component's shadow root. Moving from surrounding text onto a link does not deliver pointerover to the outer provider: the browser trims events whose target and relatedTarget retarget to the same shadow host. Consequently, ordinary hovers there never open previews. Entering the component directly over a link can open a preview, but moving onto surrounding text similarly hides pointerout from the provider, leaving the card stuck open. Composed ancestor lookup does not address this; pointer intent must be observed within the shadow root or on the anchor.

findings.title: Enabling sandboxing hides earlier task commits
findings.failure: If a managed session commits task changes before first enabling its local sandbox, projectionOperations.prepare initializes base_commit to the checkout's current HEAD. Passing that value here makes Review exclude all those task commits: a clean checkout shows no changes, its history disappears, and selecting an earlier task commit returns unknown_commit. The projection's initial checkout commit is not necessarily the task's upstream base.

findings.title: Base refresh can invalidate the selected base without invalidating the read
findings.failure: A Review request can read base A, then wait while refresh_base integrates upstream B and updates the projection's base_commit. The returned guard checks session and registry lifecycle only; neither changes during this refresh. Git can therefore compare the refreshed checkout against A and successfully return upstream-only changes and history. The projection base must also remain current across the Git read, or the request must retry.

findings.title: Profile extension dependencies are missing from review choices
findings.failure: A valid proposal can declare plugins in profiles/openclaw.yml under extensions without declaring them in manifest.packages. These plugins remain in the published archive and become installation requirements when adding the Claw, but review exposes no individual plugin choices for them. Attempting to exclude their package IDs is rejected as invalid_review_choices, so the creator must remove the entire profile, including unrelated agent settings, to exclude those dependencies.

findings.title: Excluding an avatar file makes the selected package invalid
findings.failure: When agent.identity.avatar references a workspace.files destination backed by an authored SVG file, the initial draft reviews successfully. Unchecking that file removes its workspace mapping but leaves agent.identity.avatar unchanged. Building the selected package then fails validation because the avatar no longer matches a workspace.files destination, preventing the creator from reviewing or publishing the Claw without that optional file.

findings.title: Enable button ignores read-only configuration
findings.failure: On a Gateway running with OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1 or OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1, plugins.list returns mutationAllowed:false. This code discards that flag and presents an admin with an enabled Turn on Skill Workshop button. Every click is rejected by the mutation handler, so the new recovery action cannot work on these installations.

findings.title: Unavailable plugin state stays stale after external changes
findings.failure: Open Workshop when its plugin is enabled but failed to load; the page shows the failed state without an enable button. If another client then disables that plugin, the method catalog still lacks skills.workshop.list and the connection client is unchanged. sync returns without rereading plugins.list, leaving the page in the failed state instead of offering to turn Workshop on. The operator must reopen or reload the page to recover.

findings.title: Preserve agent owner and creator filters for guests
findings.failure: For a session-only guest, sessions.list with ownerId set to a configured agent such as "main" now returns FORBIDDEN, even when the matching sessions are shared with that guest. creatorId has the same problem for agent-created sessions. These filters accept actor IDs, including agents, but the new check treats every value as a human profile ID and requires it to equal the viewer's profile. This breaks filtering otherwise readable sessions by their agent owner or creator.

findings.title: Cancel the staged operation, not just its awaiting caller
findings.failure: For updates using stagedPackage, stagePackageInstallUpdate already started the installation before this command scope exists. Its run() only resolves a continuation and awaits the existing promise, so subsequent installation commands retain their original AsyncLocalStorage context. SIGTERM during a long activation Doctor therefore aborts this empty scope without stopping Doctor. The updater can wait until the activation deadline with the Gateway stopped instead of promptly entering recovery.

findings.title: Keep immediate Git rollback outside the canceled forward scope
findings.failure: The new scope encloses all of updateGitInstall, including updateGitCheckout's immediate rollbackError recovery. If a signal interrupts git-checkout or arrives after checkout but before the runtime transaction is retained, rollback runs inside the now-aborted scope. Its recovery Git commands fail with 'Command process scope is closed', preventing restoration of the previous checkout. No retained transaction is available for the later finalizer to retry that restoration, so the update leaves the checkout unrecovered and the Gateway stopped.

findings.title: Snapshot cleanup blocks checkpoints on guest-owned directories
findings.failure: With a non-root Gateway and a Docker sandbox configured to run as root with capabilities, the guest can create root-owned 0755 directories containing files, including excluded node_modules outputs. The btrfs snapshot preserves that ownership. Canonical capture succeeds, but the Gateway cannot unlink files inside those snapshot directories, and the permission-repair helper cannot grant itself ownership rights. This awaited cleanup therefore fails the completed command with EACCES. The leftover capture also blocks subsequent checkpoints because preparation requires deleting it first. Previously, excluded outputs did not need to be recursively deleted during checkpointing.

findings.title: Tool activity text loses contrast in light themes
findings.failure: In Absolutely Light, resting tool labels and file links drop from about 4.6:1 to 3.6:1 against the transcript background. Beacon Light drops from about 7.5:1 to 5.6:1, and the new secondary color gives directory hints and subagent status text about 2.8:1. Users who rely on those themes for readability get harder-to-read narration and status text.

findings.title: Handoff disclosure arrows disappear in every state
findings.failure: When a run waits on multiple child sessions or resumes after a handoff, the session-list button uses the shared chevron class without any of the classes targeted by the reveal rules. Its arrow stays invisible when collapsed, expanded, hovered, or keyboard-focused, so users lose the visual cue that they can open or close the list.

findings.title: Bubble-mode activity disclosures lose their touch padding
findings.failure: On a touchscreen in bubble mode, the more specific zero-padding rule overrides the 8px top and bottom padding for coarse pointers. At the default text scale, a completed activity or “Worked for” disclosure shrinks from a roughly 35px-tall tap target to about 20px. Its collapsed arrow is also hidden before the first tap, making the control harder to spot and activate.

findings.title: Bubble-mode disclosures stretch across the transcript
findings.failure: In bubble mode, the summary button has width auto. Making its parent a grid stretches the button across the activity column. A short live status now appears centered inside a wide bordered bar, and tapping blank space far beyond a completed activity label toggles its details.

findings.title: Node discovery can stall the Gateway with Tool Search disabled
findings.failure: On a Bun-hosted Gateway, the first ordinary agent turn with Tool Search disabled or unset still probes for Node because the default mode is code. Each candidate runs synchronously with its own five-second timeout. A stale Node shim that hangs can freeze the Gateway for five seconds, delaying unrelated requests as well as the current turn. Multiple hanging candidates compound the delay.

findings.title: Cached Node paths survive installation and upgrade changes
findings.failure: If a Bun Gateway probes before Node is installed, installing a compatible Node into a directory already on PATH leaves Tool Search in structured mode. If a package upgrade removes the cached executable and puts a working replacement elsewhere on the same PATH, the Gateway keeps advertising code mode and calls fail with ENOENT. Both results persist across config reloads because the cache key stays the same.

findings.title: Node version-manager shims lose their launch environment
findings.failure: When the only compatible Node is exposed through an asdf shim that resolves the asdf command through PATH, invoking node from the operator's shell works. The probe strips PATH and version-manager settings, so the shim cannot find asdf in a directory such as /opt/homebrew/bin. The Gateway silently falls back to structured Tool Search despite having a compatible Node available.

findings.title: Startup output is accepted as part of the executable path
findings.failure: If an earlier node launcher on PATH prints a startup notice to stdout before forwarding to a compatible Node, the resolver caches the notice and the reported executable path as one string. It stops searching even if a plain Node executable appears later on PATH. The Gateway advertises tool_search_code, but calls fail because the cached string is not an executable path.

findings.title: Warmed memory readers bypass newly recorded quarantine
findings.failure: If a search worker has already opened an agent database and the Gateway verifier then quarantines that same file, a queued curated recall request can still return snippets from it. The verifier closes handles and sets the terminal latch in the Gateway isolate. The worker keeps its own handle and checks only the file identity and its worker-local latch when borrowing it again. If the corruption is outside the memory tables, the curated query can succeed and supply snippets to automatic recall even after quarantine has been recorded. The previous fresh-open path checked the persisted quarantine before running the query.

findings.title: A cancelled steer can keep influencing the backing run
findings.failure: An active runtime accepts a steer, the Gateway acknowledges it, and the user aborts the steer before its transcript commit is confirmed. If the runtime has already consumed the steer and cannot withdraw it, it returns an accepted but unconfirmed outcome. The new work-admission check throws on the source abort before injection finalization can stop the backing run. The user sees the steer as cancelled while the backing run can continue using its text.

findings.title: Skill preparation can lose an acknowledged first message
findings.failure: When an attributed user sends the first ordinary message to a session key with no stored row, the Gateway can return `status: started` without staging the input or committing a transcript receipt. If skill selection then fails, for example because a concurrent library edit invalidates the read, dispatch never reaches session initialization. The error fallback requires an existing session row or a prepared initial row, so the user gets a run error and their acknowledged message is missing from history. Previously this selection failure rejected the request before acknowledgement.

findings.title: An accepted steer blocks later follow-up admission
findings.failure: The handler reserves a FIFO ticket even after the active runtime has accepted a steer. If that runtime is still inside a long tool call, it can take up to two minutes to confirm the steer in the transcript. A subsequent `queueMode: followup` send can receive `status: started` but remain blocked outside the follow-up queue until the steer settles. Before the change, accepted steers did not take a reply-admission ticket, so the follow-up could be queued while the active run was still working.

findings.title: Aborting skill preparation leaves later sends blocked
findings.failure: If a skill-library read stalls after acknowledgement and the user aborts that run, the Gateway publishes the abort but the read has no run abort signal and the FIFO ticket is released only when dispatch unwinds. A subsequent send to the same session can be acknowledged and finish its own preparation, yet still wait for the cancelled run's read to return or time out.

findings.title: Slow-send diagnostics miss WebSocket work before the handler
findings.failure: WebSocket requests resolve `expectedProfileId` and may wait for transport admission before calling `handleGatewayRequest`. The new timer starts inside that call. If either earlier step takes several seconds and the handler responds in under a second, the operator sees a slow acknowledgement with no `slow chat send` request record, and the new phase metrics omit the delay.

findings.title: Transparent footer intercepts clicks on visible transcript links
findings.failure: In a desktop chat with a centered composer notice, scroll until a message link sits beside the notice in the bottom 28–35 pixels of the transcript. The link is visible, but the full-width footer sits above it and receives the click. The link opens only after the user scrolls it above the overlap.

findings.title: Composer clips the history Retry button in short panes
findings.failure: Open a conversation whose history fails to load and has no cached messages, in a pane short enough that the error screen must scroll. The fallback uses its own scroll container and receives none of the new transcript bottom padding. Even at the bottom of its scroll range, the composer can cover most of the Retry button when the error text wraps.

findings.title: Scroll to latest can cover a mobile Goal pill
findings.failure: In a short mobile pane with a pending approval and a Goal pill that reaches the center, the approval can shrink while the pill keeps its full height. Clearance is tested against the button position before the overlap offset is applied. The test can miss the pill, then CSS raises the button into it. When the user has scrolled up, tapping the covered part of the Goal pill jumps to the latest message instead of opening the goal.

findings.title: Storage-only tool details can prevent finalization
findings.failure: A plugin tool can return a short success receipt with a diagnostic details field larger than the finalizer's byte limit. The live tool result retains those details, while durable model-context hydration strips them. The new sizing pass counts the details before replay cleanup, and replacing the result body leaves them in place. If this is the last tool result and the model then returns an empty answer, the selector cannot retain the completed tool frame. Finalization fails before contacting the provider, leaving the user without a summary of the completed work.

findings.title: A legacy message timestamp can abort finalization
findings.failure: An imported transcript can contain a historical user message with a valid entry timestamp and no timestamp inside the message payload. Session hydration preserves that payload, and a provider such as OpenAI Responses can replay its text. When a later tool turn needs finalization, converting the missing payload timestamp to ISO throws before the selector can even decide whether to retain that row. The completed tool turn gets no final answer.

findings.title: Finalization can discard the active compaction summary
findings.failure: A compacted session can start a tool turn with a summary and retained history that fit the byte limit, then exceed that limit after the current request and completed tool exchanges are added. Durable hydration reserves space for the compaction summary before selecting the recent suffix. The new wrapper labels the summary as an ordinary message, so the suffix cut can discard it even when the summary and current turn fit together. The finalizer can then answer without decisions or constraints recorded only in that summary.

findings.title: PostgreSQL still cannot finalize jobs with escaped NULs in their definitions
findings.failure: A retained one-shot job can be created with a NUL in its agent prompt. The cron store serializes it as an escaped \u0000 in the PostgreSQL text column. When the run finishes, the new enablement update casts the entire definition to jsonb, which rejects that escape even though the update only changes the enabled flag. The finalization transaction rolls back, leaving the job marked as running and its terminal result absent from history.

findings.title: Systems machine picker loses its keyboard focus indicator
findings.failure: At viewport widths of 768px or less, tabbing to the Systems machine picker in standard color mode produces no visible focus indicator. The new shared class removes the focus outline, and the more specific Systems border rule overrides the shared focus border color.

findings.title: Long camera and microphone names become indistinguishable
findings.failure: On a wide screen in a browser that supports customizable selects, two camera or microphone labels that share a long prefix and differ only at the end can appear identical in Settings. The popup previously had room to grow with the labels. It now stops at the 340px trigger minimum, clips the distinguishing suffixes, and the device options have no tooltip that reveals the full names.

findings.title: The chevron overlaps selected text in right-to-left layouts
findings.failure: With Arabic or Persian selected in a browser that supports customizable selects, the chevron moves to the left but the extra padding stays on the right. A long selected value, such as a session group name, can extend under the chevron and obscure the end of the visible label or its ellipsis.

findings.title: The desktop sizing control truncates short mode labels on phones
findings.failure: In the touch desktop viewer at a 430px viewport width, the sizing select remains 88px wide. The new shared padding and 16px touch font leave only 42px for the selected label, so an English mode such as Actual can appear truncated even though it fit with the previous native control.

findings.title: Restart drops user turns in previously spawned dashboard chats
findings.failure: After a visible spawned task finishes, a user can reopen its dashboard chat and start a new turn. If the Gateway restarts during that turn, the session's original `createdVia: "spawn"` stamp prevents shutdown from saving a recovery marker and startup from recovering the turn. The user's follow-up no longer resumes as it did before the change.

findings.title: Upgrade closes legacy paused tasks that still accept continuations
findings.failure: A paused native child saved by an older release can have neither a `waitForMessage` flag nor descendants. Its controlling requester could previously resume that exact task with `sessions_send`. After upgrade, the first sweep classifies the restored row as unreachable and settles it, so the requester loses the ability to continue the original task even when the requester is still present.

findings.title: Failed nested handoff leaves the enclosing requester waiting
findings.failure: If a root yields for child A and A yields for child B, a permanent rejection of B's handoff marks A's session failed but leaves A's registry run paused. The lifecycle write updates the session row without settling the native task, and the sweeper's descendant-loss check applies only to retired runs. The root can still see A as waiting and never receive A's terminal result.

findings.title: Retry loses the failure notice after the lifecycle commits
findings.failure: If the requester lifecycle commits as failed but the separate transcript append hits a transient write error, settlement retries the lifecycle event. The `requireYielded` check now rejects it because the run is already failed, so the retry completes without appending the classified guidance. The user sees the failed state without the notice explaining how to recover the child work.

findings.title: A failed restart notice strands accepted queued messages
findings.failure: When a yielded session has lost its child source and its restart marker contains accepted queued inputs, startup clears the marker before recording the yield failure. If recording that failure throws, startup skips the queued-input continuation. The messages are left unprocessed, and a later startup has no marker identifying them as inputs to resume.

findings.title: Windows short-path caches can block SQLite snapshots
findings.failure: When LOCALAPPDATA or an explicit staging root uses a Windows 8.3 path such as C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local, the staging directory keeps that spelling. The guarded copier compares ordinary and native realpaths, which can interpret the short spelling and its expanded spelling as a moved root. Strict update or Doctor inspection then fails even though the database is stable and the cache is writable.

findings.title: Normal rollback-journal deletion can abort inspection
findings.failure: If a SQLite writer commits and deletes its rollback journal after the snapshot pins and resolves the journal but before the guarded helper reopens it, the helper throws a terminal error. The previous copier could read the pinned descriptor and then retry after detecting that the journal had disappeared. Strict inspection now fails even when the database has already settled and a fresh attempt could inspect it.

findings.title: Large histories can exhaust temporary storage during bounded hydration
findings.failure: On PostgreSQL with a finite temp_file_limit, a session with enough unrelated custom events to exceed work_mem and the temporary-file allowance now fails to hydrate even a small context window. The CTE stores navigation rows for all those events before the outer predicates reject them. Previously the dependency query could reject each of those rows before storing it for the final sort.

findings.title: SQLite hydration warnings report zero statement time on the regular reader
findings.failure: On a normal SQLite Gateway, a bounded cron hydration worker opens a native read-only connection without observeConnection(). The inherited hydration label starts the timer, but the connection never feeds it statement measurements. A slow read therefore logs statementExecutionMs as 0 and an empty statement summary, attributing the query time to callbackOtherMs. The benchmark wraps its connection explicitly, so it bypasses this failure.

findings.title: Applying a browsed replacement can silently keep the old folder
findings.failure: An admin selects a device folder, reopens the browser to replace it, and the device loses its last available worker slot while the picker is open. Use this folder remains enabled, but selectDeviceFolder rejects the change because the device is no longer selectable. The browser still closes. When a slot frees up, Start uses the old folder. The previous code still updated an existing selection in this situation.

findings.title: Background updates erase an unsubmitted manual path
findings.failure: While an operator types a path, an unrelated New Session update such as an agent roster refresh rebuilds the picker params. The writable signal re-derives from the saved selection and replaces the typed text with the previous path or an empty field. The editor stays open, so the operator can lose the edit without dismissing it.

findings.title: Touch users cannot verify the full folder path before retrying
findings.failure: After a pending device-folder session is restored on a phone, the picker trigger is disabled and shows only the final folder name. The full path is available through hover or assistive technology, so a sighted touch user cannot tell whether a retry will use /srv/client-a/project or /srv/client-b/project. The previous disabled field displayed the saved path directly.

findings.title: Hover sends a prefilled update report to GitHub
findings.failure: When update reporting falls back to a prefilled GitHub issue and its URL is at most 2,048 characters, hovering or keyboard-focusing Open prefilled issue sends the URL through the Gateway to GitHub. The query contains the full report title and diagnostic body, so GitHub receives them even if the operator leaves without opening the issue form.

findings.title: Hover and focus changes inside the link reader go unnoticed
findings.failure: Links in a GitHub issue body are inside the link reader panel's shadow root. When the pointer moves from issue text onto a link, or keyboard focus moves between controls in that same root, the browser keeps the transition events inside the root. The provider's outside listeners miss them, so previews can fail to open. If a preview was opened by entering the link from outside the root, moving onto nearby issue text can leave the preview open and allow a brief hover to trigger a fetch.

findings.title: Hovercards lose their styles inside shadow-root modals
findings.failure: Hovering Open original in a chat lightbox for an external image or video mounts the preview inside the lightbox's shadow root. The document stylesheet cannot reach the card there, even after popover promotion. The preview uses browser-default layout and loses its intended width, height, and image sizing.

findings.title: Empty previews hide authored link hints
findings.failure: After the hover runtime loads, a Markdown link with a title such as Requires administrator access loses that hint whenever public preview is enabled. If the destination has no metadata or the request fails, the card falls back to the visible link text and hostname, leaving the authored warning unavailable on both hover and keyboard focus.

findings.title: Review shows upstream changes after an already-current base refresh
findings.failure: If an operator fetches a newer default-branch tip and rebases the managed task onto it, `refresh_base` sees that tip in HEAD's ancestry and returns `current` without updating the projection's `base_commit`. Review now uses the older stored SHA even though the default-branch ref is up to date. The file list, ahead count, and commit picker include upstream changes that the previous merge-base calculation excluded.

findings.title: Concurrent refresh can pair an old base with the refreshed checkout
findings.failure: If Review reads the projection just before `refresh_base` accepts a new base, and its queued Git read starts after the refresh finishes, it compares the refreshed checkout to the old SHA. Refresh changes neither the session binding nor the registry identity, so both final guards pass. Review can return upstream-only files and commits in the task diff.

findings.title: Archived Review reports an ownership error after normal cleanup
findings.failure: Archiving a projected session preserves its worktree binding. Background cleanup then removes the checkout and marks its registry record removed while retaining the projection for recovery. An authorized Review request now fails with `Local workspace review owner changed`. Previously the missing checkout returned `not_git`, which the panel displays as an unavailable-checkout message.

findings.title: Review applies the outer repository's base to a nested checkout
findings.failure: Worktree preparation supports a session whose cwd is a subdirectory of the managed checkout. If that directory becomes a separate Git checkout after the projection is created, the path containment check still passes. Git resolves the nested repository from the session cwd, but Review supplies the outer repository's SHA. When that SHA is absent from the nested repository, All changes fails with `Unable to read tracked Git changes`. Previously Review used the nested repository's own refs.

findings.title: Loading rings disappear under same-origin-only image policies
findings.failure: If a reverse proxy adds an `img-src 'self'` Content Security Policy, the browser blocks the new `data:` SVG masks even though the Gateway's own policy allows them. The affected spinners previously rendered with CSS borders. After the change, the chat Send button can appear blank while a send is pending, and running-session rings disappear from the sidebar.

findings.title: Publication uses the Gateway's ClawHub account
findings.failure: If a creator uses a shared Gateway whose environment token or saved ClawHub login belongs to someone else, review and publish both use that host credential. The creator sees the other account as publisher and can publish an immutable version under that account.

findings.title: Headless administrator clients can publish
findings.failure: A headless client with a live authenticated administrator WebSocket passes the same check as the Control UI. It can request a review token and publish in sequence with no person opening the review or confirming publication in the UI.

findings.title: Drafts are created outside the source session's worktree
findings.failure: When the source chat runs in a local worktree, the Gateway creates the draft in the agent's configured workspace. The generated command gives the agent a relative path, which resolves inside the worktree. The agent either cannot open the draft or writes a separate copy, leaving the Gateway to review the untouched starter document.

findings.title: Profile extensions are missing from dependency choices
findings.failure: A draft with a plugin declared only in the OpenClaw profile includes that dependency in the archive, and Add resolves it as a plugin. The creator gets no checkbox for that plugin and has to discard the entire profile, including unrelated settings, to remove it through review.

findings.title: Excluding the avatar file breaks review
findings.failure: After a valid draft maps a file such as avatar.svg to the agent's workspace avatar, unchecking that file removes its workspace mapping but leaves the avatar reference in the manifest. The builder rejects the selection, so the creator cannot get a fresh review token without editing the proposal.

findings.title: Excluding the profile can leave a broken metadata reference
findings.failure: A valid manifest can point to profiles/openclaw.yml through the supported legacy openclaw.config metadata key. Unchecking that profile removes the file but retains the pointer, so the next review fails when the builder tries to open the deleted profile.

findings.title: A UTF-8 BOM makes every draft save look stale
findings.failure: If an editor writes the draft with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, the read method strips it before calculating the revision. Save compares that revision with a hash of the original bytes, including the mark. An unchanged draft therefore produces a conflict even immediately after reloading.

findings.title: Base refresh can apply private files after the requester loses repository access
findings.failure: A linked guest starts refreshing their prepared PR in a private repository. If their GitHub repository access is revoked during the base fetch while the managed publisher retains access, the final check still passes. It rechecks the publisher's write eligibility and the guest's local account link, then applies the fetched private target files to the guest's workspace.

findings.title: Base refresh overwrites a staged deletion when a working copy exists
findings.failure: In a prepared workspace, a guest uses git rm --cached on a tracked file and keeps an edited working copy. Git reports the staged deletion and the untracked copy as separate records, so the partial-staging guard lets refresh proceed. The final git add -A stages the working copy and replaces the guest's staged deletion.

findings.title: Merging the PR on GitHub strands pending local base conflicts
findings.failure: A base refresh conflicts with unpublished guest edits while the remote PR remains mergeable. If someone merges the PR on GitHub before the guest acknowledges the local resolution, refresh_base rejects the merged PR before it reaches recovery. The canonical workspace keeps MERGE_HEAD, so archive and eviction still reject it and tell the operator to finish the integration.

findings.title: Refreshing after a fork rename leaves publication targeting stale repository metadata
findings.failure: After an external fork PR is prepared, rename its head repository without changing its branch or commit, then advance the target and run refresh_base. Refresh succeeds because the repository ID is unchanged, but it saves the new base with the old head repository name. Publication rejects the saved target, and prepare_pr takes its same-head, same-base shortcut without repairing the name.

findings.title: Doctor overrides intentionally restrictive allowlists
findings.failure: An operator who hand-writes a config for the plugin-based release with `plugins.allow: ["memory-core"]` to keep Workshop off will have Workshop enabled the next time they run `openclaw doctor --fix`. The migration treats every unmarked restrictive allowlist as built-in-era policy, so it adds `skill-workshop` even when the operator deliberately excluded it after the plugin returned.

findings.title: Normal Gateway startup skips the allowlist migration
findings.failure: An operator who upgrades outside `openclaw update` and starts the Gateway with an otherwise valid built-in-era config such as `plugins.allow: ["memory-core"]` still loses Workshop. The startup preflight accepts the valid config without running this Doctor migration, so Workshop stays off and learned skills disappear from agent prompts until the operator repairs the config.

findings.title: Workshop offers an enable button that policy always rejects
findings.failure: An admin sees Turn on Skill Workshop even when `plugins.enabled` is false, a current `plugins.deny` includes `skill-workshop`, or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` makes the config immutable. In each case the Gateway refuses the request and the page re-enables the same button, so every click fails until the underlying policy changes.

findings.title: Availability stays stale when Workshop methods remain absent
findings.failure: If Workshop is enabled but failed to load, the open page displays the load-failure state. Disabling the plugin from another client publishes a new plugin generation, but the Workshop method is absent both before and after that change. The page keeps the same client and skips rereading `plugins.list`, so it still says Workshop is turned on and gives the admin no enable button until they reopen the page.

findings.title: A failed capability refresh leaves the enable button stuck
findings.failure: If `plugins.setEnabled` succeeds but the event-triggered `plugins.uiDescriptors` request times out, the Gateway has enabled Workshop while the page still has the old method catalog. The success path leaves the button disabled on “Turning on…” and offers no retry, so the Workshop never loads on that connection unless a later capability refresh succeeds.

findings.title: An older ambiguous tool result blocks a valid recent context
findings.failure: If two older calls share an ID and a displaced result matches both, a size limit can cut away just one of those calls. The reader then rejects the entire context because the result would gain an owner. It rejects even when a shorter suffix containing a newer complete tool frame and the latest user message fits. Codex consequently fails before submitting the next turn.

findings.title: A history read failure suppresses successful compaction reporting
findings.failure: If Codex completes native compaction after the current turn adds a mirrored message or tool frame that exceeds the history budget, the completion handler's history read throws. The notification controller only logs the exception at debug level. The handler skips the after-compaction hook, the transcript activity entry, and the compaction-end event, so the session can omit a compaction that actually completed.

findings.title: An empty branch summary can erase the bounded context
findings.failure: A caller can append a short user message followed by a branch summary with an empty summary string. With maxEvents set to 1 and enough bytes for either entry, the bounded reader spends the only slot on the summary. The context builder skips empty branch summaries, so the caller receives an empty message list even though the latest visible message fits.

findings.title: Foreign-filter response reveals whether an agent has hidden sessions
findings.failure: On the cached WebSocket list path, a session-only guest who supplies a foreign ownerId and an agentId gets a successful empty result when the configured agent has no sessions. Once another user creates a draft on that agent, the same request returns FORBIDDEN even though the draft is invisible to the guest. Empty partitions skip authorization, while nonempty partitions run it before checking row visibility.

findings.title: Person privacy check blocks filters for agent-owned sessions
findings.failure: A session-only guest can see a shared session whose assigned owner is the agent main, but filtering the list by ownerId main now returns FORBIDDEN with a message about other people's activity. The existing owner filter accepts agent identities, and the new guard treats every owner ID as a human profile ID.

findings.title: Saved owner filter leaves the sidebar on a denied query after demotion
findings.failure: A member who saves another person's sidebar owner filter keeps that preference after becoming a guest. In the agent-chip sidebar, the restored filter now produces FORBIDDEN, and the automatic reset requires a successful result from that same query. The sidebar stays on the failed filter across reloads until the user manually chooses a different owner filter.

findings.title: Everyone shows the guest's personal session count
findings.failure: If a guest can see two shared sessions and is associated with only one, the Activity people picker shows 1 next to Everyone even though choosing Everyone shows both sessions. The picker uses peopleSessionCount for the full time window, but the new calculation counts only sessions associated with the guest.

findings.title: A valid default legacy memory index prevents recovery capture from sealing
findings.failure: When a valid legacy index exists at stateDir/memory/main.sqlite, the retry inventory also declares main.sqlite-wal, main.sqlite-shm, and main.sqlite-journal as recovery roots, even when those files are absent. The backup consolidates the SQLite database and strips companion entries from the manifest while retaining their roots. Manifest validation rejects the entire capture with “Update recovery manifest is missing a root entry.” Doctor or the updater can then proceed without a pre-migration recovery copy.

findings.title: An empty legacy .sqlite placeholder aborts the entire recovery capture
findings.failure: When a configured legacy memory index points to a zero-byte file named main.sqlite, declaring it as kind file still sends it through the SQLite snapshot path because the backup classifier recognizes the .sqlite suffix before checking the header. The snapshot requires a nonempty source and aborts the entire capture. Doctor can then continue and delete the placeholder without a sealed recovery copy of the rest of the pre-repair state.

findings.title: Jump to latest can stay hidden while a reply grows
findings.failure: If a history refresh introduces a new user message and buffered reply text together, the transcript anchors to the question and clears the flag that shows Jump to latest. Subsequent chunks of already-visible reply text no longer trigger the timeline update that sets the flag. The reply can grow below the viewport while the button stays hidden until another timeline event or a manual scroll.

findings.title: A saved reply can appear alongside its stale streaming prefix
findings.failure: If the live bubble shows “Hello” and the stream has already received “Hello world,” a saved “Hello world” message arriving before the next display update is compared against “Hello.” The transcript shows both the full reply and its stale prefix until the display update or a terminal event clears the live bubble. Touch tracking can defer that display update.

findings.title: Interrupting Git activation also cancels checkout rollback
findings.failure: On a managed Git install, send SIGTERM after checkout changes HEAD but before the runner registers its rollback transaction, for example while it sets the new dev branch's upstream. The new scope cancels the Git runner's recovery commands along with its forward commands. The checkout can stay on the candidate commit, and without a verified source rollback or a retained transaction the updater leaves the Gateway stopped.

findings.title: Post-stop config validation disables signal recovery
findings.failure: If the config changes while the Gateway is stopping, the post-stop refresh reruns candidate validation. The ledger correctly keeps the phase at activating, but the signal tracker stores the requested validating phase. A SIGTERM during that rehearsal takes the pre-activation exit path, seals compensation, and can leave the Gateway stopped.

findings.title: Migrated finalization can complete successfully after interruption
findings.failure: If the installed updater receives SIGTERM while the candidate worker owns finalization after a schema migration, the worker is outside the tracked forward scopes and receives no interruption. It can keep mutating state, start the candidate Gateway, and publish a success report even though the parent announced an interruption and exits with code 143.

findings.title: Staged updates keep running activation commands after a signal
findings.failure: For an update using an explicit package artifact, the staging code starts the install pipeline before this cancellation scope exists. Calling run here resumes and awaits that existing pipeline, so a SIGTERM sent to the updater during the staged candidate's activation Doctor does not reach the Doctor process. The Gateway can remain down while recovery waits for Doctor to finish or for the signal recovery budget to expire.

findings.title: A signal during final history capture can produce a success report
findings.failure: After a successful restart, send SIGTERM while the updater is awaiting capture of the completed history record. The signal handler still accepts the signal as a verification interruption, but the pending result was already computed and terminal publication never checks it again. The updater can save a success report without the signal and then exit with code 143.

findings.title: Codex can escape orphan cleanup after the launcher replaces itself
findings.failure: With the new execve launcher on POSIX, process registration can read and hash the Node launcher's command line before it replaces itself with Codex at the same PID. If the Gateway is then killed while that app-server is still alive, the next Gateway sees the native command line, treats it as a different process, and deletes the registration without reaping the old app-server or its descendants.

findings.title: Inline-command benchmarks reject the bundled Codex version
findings.failure: When an operator selects a checkout containing this change as the candidate for either inline-command benchmark, the verifier reads the installed Codex version as 0.169.0 and asserts that it is 0.164.0. Both benchmark entry points abort before collecting measurements, even when the candidate is the only selected cell.

findings.title: Execve launch errors are missed for escaped installation paths
findings.failure: If a POSIX installation path contains a literal backslash and the bundled binary lacks execute permission, Node escapes the backslash in the printed EACCES path. The observer compares that escaped text with the literal filesystem path, so the operator gets a generic startup failure and later requests retry the same unusable binary instead of using the recorded launch failure.

findings.title: Plugin inspection fills the temporary volume before capacity selection
findings.failure: If an operator sets TMPDIR to a small volume and an enabled plugin imports a dependency with a large data payload, inventory now materializes that dependency on the temporary volume before reporting its size. The worker can fail with ENOSPC before the updater gets a chance to select the state volume, even when that volume has ample space for the rehearsal.

findings.title: An unusable Doctor contract can now block the entire update
findings.failure: A disabled custom plugin can still have a declared Doctor contract. If that contract imports a package alias whose imports target is invalid, such as a target starting with ../, the new inspection propagates ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_TARGET and aborts candidate Doctor. Previously Doctor caught the contract load failure and continued, so the disabled plugin could remain installed during an update.

findings.title: Repair rejects imports through the staged OpenClaw host link
findings.failure: A plugin that imports a host module by a relative path through its node_modules/openclaw link worked in a published-driver snapshot because the copier points that link at the staged candidate. Repair resolves the import to the staged host outside the private state directory and rejects it as an escape, blocking the update even when the snapshot is complete.

findings.title: Relative imports break when they cross the managed state projection
findings.failure: If a plugin at STATE/extensions/demo imports ../../shared/value.mjs from STATE/shared, inventory finds the helper but places it under candidate-plugins while the plugin is copied to REHEARSAL/extensions/demo. The unchanged import looks in REHEARSAL/shared, so the plugin still fails to load despite the helper being copied.

findings.title: Sibling imports lose symlink names outside the plugin directory
findings.failure: If a plugin imports ../shared/value.mjs and that path is a symlink to ../lib/value.mjs, inspection returns the canonical file without the sibling symlink. Neither the fresh copy nor published-snapshot repair creates shared/value.mjs in the rehearsal, so the original module specifier still fails to resolve.

findings.title: Stopping the last nested task leaves the turn open
findings.failure: When a background parent has already returned its answer and its nested Agent or Workflow is the only remaining hold, the runtime emits the parent's answer as interim. If Claude then reports the child as stopped, this branch clears the hold, but turn settlement still requires a later result. Stopped tasks produce no follow-up result, so the turn stays active until the watchdog fires.

findings.title: Repair closes remapped operations without verifying the previous installation
findings.failure: If an update stops in prepared or before displacement in publishing, a remount leaves the previous package installed under its projected identity. The fallback guard compares the live identity with the unprojected identities and falls through. Neither verification branch runs, so repair archives the unfinished operation and clears the update block without checking the previous tree or its launchers. If the lease is unchanged, it also reports a manual replacement that never happened.

findings.title: Repair rejects hot SQLite journals before replay can run
findings.failure: If the updater dies during a SQLite commit, readForRecovery can recover the committed record from a snapshot while leaving the live rollback journal for replay under the executor fence. The new inspectRemount call rereads the live database before that replay. SQLite returns SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK, so public repair aborts and leaves the journal blocking recovery, even when the filesystem device numbers are unchanged.

findings.title: Repair rejects launchers published by the updater
findings.failure: When publication copies a launcher into place, the installed launcher gets a different inode from the staged launcher. The updater records that inode in publications, or in the launcher intent if it is interrupted before acknowledgement. After a remount, repair ignores both records and compares the installed inode with the previous or staged inode. It rejects an intact installed candidate with an inode-mapping error and leaves the journal active.

findings.title: Repair rejects newer releases after some supported update targets
findings.failure: An interrupted update can record an explicit target such as 2026.9.4-dev.1. If the operator then manually installs 2026.10.1 after a remount, the release comparator returns null because it excludes dev prereleases. Repair reports that it requires a newer manual installation and leaves the journal active without verifying the newer package.

findings.title: Starting dictation hides its recording border
findings.failure: When a user starts voice dictation in New Session, the drop overlay and the recording border both target the message box’s ::after pseudo-element. The more specific drop rule forces its opacity to zero whenever no file is being dragged, so the recording border disappears while the microphone is active.

findings.title: Environment controls lose parts of their keyboard focus rings
findings.failure: Expand Environment and Tab to the machine selector or the Changes button. The section keeps its body at overflow: hidden even after it settles. The widened rows extend 4 px past both sides of that body, so it clips the left and right sides of the focused button’s outline. Those sides previously fit inside the body.

findings.title: Task Progress failures use the ordinary status color
findings.failure: Open desktop Details for a task whose run failed or whose delegated work reports a failed child. The runtime status is marked as an error, but the new selector overrides its danger color with muted text. The failure message and any error detail look like routine status text.

findings.title: Subagent summary icons overlap
findings.failure: Expand Subagents for a session with six or more subagents. The summary still overlaps its avatar slots by 6 px, but the shared row rule shrinks each slot to 16 px and enlarges each bot glyph to 15 px. Adjacent glyphs now intersect, and the transparent avatar backgrounds expose the intersecting strokes.

findings.title: Snapshots can delete canonical files backed by host mounts
findings.failure: Bind-mount a directory containing an already accepted file over an ordinary empty directory inside the btrfs projection, then edit a different file. The live scan can see the mounted file, but the btrfs snapshot contains the underlying empty directory. That directory has no inode-2 marker, so checkpointing treats the missing file as a guest deletion and removes it from the canonical worktree even though it remains visible in the guest.

findings.title: Foreign-owned snapshot directories can block all later checkpoints
findings.failure: A non-root Gateway can read a guest-created directory owned by another UID, such as a root-owned 0755 directory created through a writable rootful Docker sandbox. The snapshot preserves that ownership. Cleanup cannot unlink files inside the directory, and the repair skips chmod because the owner's mode bits already include 0700. The command reports a checkpoint failure after its edits have reached canonical storage. Subsequent checkpoints fail while removing the same leftover snapshot, even if the directory is removed from the live guest.

findings.title: Native benchmark loses its report on a standard cgroup v2 host
findings.failure: Run the native benchmark directly on a Linux host where /sys/fs/cgroup exposes the actual cgroup v2 root. Its cpu.stat exists, so the script enables CPU accounting, but root cgroups have no cpu.max. After the measured commands complete, the report builder throws ENOENT and the operator gets no benchmark report.
